translations.kjv: And he went through Syria and Cilicia, confirming the churches.
translations.ylt: and he went through Syria and Cilicia, confirming the assemblies.
translations.web: He went through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the assemblies.

translations.kjv: Then came he to Derbe and Lystra: and, behold, a certain disciple was there, named Timotheus, the son of a certain woman, which was a Jewess, and believed; but his father was a Greek:
translations.ylt: And he came to Derbe and Lystra, and lo, a certain disciple was there, by name Timotheus son of a certain woman, a believing Jewess, but of a father, a Greek,
translations.web: He came to Derbe and Lystra; and behold, a certain disciple was there, named Timothy, the son of a Jewess who believed, but his father was a Greek.

translations.kjv: Which was well reported of by the brethren that were at Lystra and Iconium.
translations.ylt: who was well testified to by the brethren in Lystra and Iconium;
translations.web: The brothers who were at Lystra and Iconium gave a good testimony about him.

translations.kjv: Him would Paul have to go forth with him; and took and circumcised him because of the Jews which were in those quarters: for they knew all that his father was a Greek.
translations.ylt: this one did Paul wish to go forth with him, and having taken him, he circumcised him, because of the Jews who are in those places, for they all knew his father--that he was a Greek.
translations.web: Paul wanted to have him go out with him, and he took and circumcised him because of the Jews who were in those parts, for they all knew that his father was a Greek.

translations.kjv: And as they went through the cities, they delivered them the decrees for to keep, that were ordained of the apostles and elders which were at Jerusalem.
translations.ylt: And as they were going on through the cities, they were delivering to them the decrees to keep, that have been judged by the apostles and the elders who are in Jerusalem,
translations.web: As they went on their way through the cities, they delivered the decrees to them to keep which had been ordained by the apostles and elders who were at Jerusalem.

translations.kjv: And so were the churches established in the faith, and increased in number daily.
translations.ylt: then, indeed, were the assemblies established in the faith, and were abounding in number every day;
translations.web: So the assemblies were strengthened in the faith, and increased in number daily.

translations.kjv: Now when they had gone throughout Phrygia and the region of Galatia, and were forbidden of the Holy Ghost to preach the word in Asia,
translations.ylt: and having gone through Phrygia and the region of Galatia, having been forbidden by the Holy Spirit to speak the word in Asia,
translations.web: When they had gone through the region of Phrygia and Galatia, they were forbidden by the Holy Spirit to speak the word in Asia.

translations.kjv: After they were come to Mysia, they assayed to go into Bithynia: but the Spirit suffered them not.
translations.ylt: having gone toward Mysia, they were trying to go on toward Bithynia, and the Spirit did not suffer them,
translations.web: When they had come opposite Mysia, they tried to go into Bithynia, but the Spirit didn’t allow them.

translations.kjv: And they passing by Mysia came down to Troas.
translations.ylt: and having passed by Mysia, they came down to Troas.
translations.web: Passing by Mysia, they came down to Troas.

translations.kjv: And a vision appeared to Paul in the night; There stood a man of Macedonia, and prayed him, saying, Come over into Macedonia, and help us.
translations.ylt: And a vision through the night appeared to Paul--a certain man of Macedonia was standing, calling upon him, and saying, `Having passed through to Macedonia, help us;' --
translations.web: A vision appeared to Paul in the night. There was a man of Macedonia standing, begging him and saying, “Come over into Macedonia and help us.”

translations.kjv: And after he had seen the vision, immediately we endeavoured to go into Macedonia, assuredly gathering that the Lord had called us for to preach the gospel unto them.
translations.ylt: and when he saw the vision, immediately we endeavoured to go forth to Macedonia, assuredly gathering that the Lord hath called us to preach good news to them,
translations.web: When he had seen the vision, immediately we sought to go out to Macedonia, concluding that the Lord had called us to preach the Good News to them.

translations.kjv: Therefore loosing from Troas, we came with a straight course to Samothracia, and the next day to Neapolis;
translations.ylt: having set sail, therefore, from Troas, we came with a straight course to Samothracia, on the morrow also to Neapolis,
translations.web: Setting sail therefore from Troas, we made a straight course to Samothrace, and the day following to Neapolis;

translations.kjv: And from thence to Philippi, which is the chief city of that part of Macedonia, and a colony: and we were in that city abiding certain days.
translations.ylt: thence also to Philippi, which is a principal city of the part of Macedonia--a colony. And we were in this city abiding certain days,
translations.web: and from there to Philippi, which is a city of Macedonia, the foremost of the district, a Roman colony. We were staying some days in this city.

translations.kjv: And on the sabbath we went out of the city by a river side, where prayer was wont to be made; and we sat down, and spake unto the women which resorted thither.
translations.ylt: on the sabbath-day also we went forth outside of the city, by a river, where there used to be prayer, and having sat down, we were speaking to the women who came together,
translations.web: On the Sabbath day we went outside of the city by a riverside, where we supposed there was a place of prayer, and we sat down and spoke to the women who had come together.

translations.kjv: And a certain woman named Lydia, a seller of purple, of the city of Thyatira, which worshipped God, heard us: whose heart the Lord opened, that she attended unto the things which were spoken of Paul.
translations.ylt: and a certain woman, by name Lydia, a seller of purple, of the city of Thyatira, worshipping God, was hearing, whose heart the Lord did open to attend to the things spoken by Paul;
translations.web: A certain woman named Lydia, a seller of purple, of the city of Thyatira, one who worshiped God, heard us. The Lord opened her heart to listen to the things which were spoken by Paul.

translations.kjv: And when she was baptized, and her household, she besought us, saying, If ye have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, come into my house, and abide there. And she constrained us.
translations.ylt: and when she was baptized, and her household, she did call upon us, saying, `If ye have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, having entered into my house, remain;' and she constrained us.
translations.web: When she and her household were baptized, she begged us, saying, “If you have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, come into my house and stay.” So she persuaded us.

translations.kjv: And it came to pass, as we went to prayer, a certain damsel possessed with a spirit of divination met us, which brought her masters much gain by soothsaying:
translations.ylt: And it came to pass in our going on to prayer, a certain maid, having a spirit of Python, did meet us, who brought much employment to her masters by soothsaying,
translations.web: As we were going to prayer, a certain girl having a spirit of divination met us, who brought her masters much gain by fortune telling.

translations.kjv: The same followed Paul and us, and cried, saying, These men are the servants of the most high God, which shew unto us the way of salvation.
translations.ylt: she having followed Paul and us, was crying, saying, `These men are servants of the Most High God, who declare to us a way of salvation;'
translations.web: Following Paul and us, she cried out, “These men are servants of the Most High God, who proclaim to us a way of salvation!”

translations.kjv: And this did she many days. But Paul, being grieved, turned and said to the spirit, I command thee in the name of Jesus Christ to come out of her. And he came out the same hour.
translations.ylt: and this she was doing for many days, but Paul having been grieved, and having turned, said to the spirit, `I command thee, in the name of Jesus Christ, to come forth from her;' and it came forth the same hour.
translations.web: She was doing this for many days. But Paul, becoming greatly annoyed, turned and said to the spirit, “I command you in the name of Jesus Christ to come out of her!” It came out that very hour.

translations.kjv: And when her masters saw that the hope of their gains was gone, they caught Paul and Silas, and drew them into the marketplace unto the rulers,
translations.ylt: And her masters having seen that the hope of their employment was gone, having caught Paul and Silas, drew them to the market-place, unto the rulers,
translations.web: But when her masters saw that the hope of their gain was gone, they seized Paul and Silas and dragged them into the marketplace before the rulers.

translations.kjv: And brought them to the magistrates, saying, These men, being Jews, do exceedingly trouble our city,
translations.ylt: and having brought them to the magistrates, they said, `These men do exceedingly trouble our city, being Jews;
translations.web: When they had brought them to the magistrates, they said, “These men, being Jews, are agitating our city

translations.kjv: And teach customs, which are not lawful for us to receive, neither to observe, being Romans.
translations.ylt: and they proclaim customs that are not lawful for us to receive nor to do, being Romans.'
translations.web: and advocate customs which it is not lawful for us to accept or to observe, being Romans.”

translations.kjv: And the multitude rose up together against them: and the magistrates rent off their clothes, and commanded to beat them.
translations.ylt: And the multitude rose up together against them, and the magistrates having torn their garments from them, were commanding to beat them with rods,
translations.web: The multitude rose up together against them and the magistrates tore their clothes from them, then commanded them to be beaten with rods.

translations.kjv: And when they had laid many stripes upon them, they cast them into prison, charging the jailor to keep them safely:
translations.ylt: many blows also having laid upon them, they cast them to prison, having given charge to the jailor to keep them safely,
translations.web: When they had laid many stripes on them, they threw them into prison, charging the jailer to keep them safely.

translations.kjv: Who, having received such a charge, thrust them into the inner prison, and made their feet fast in the stocks.
translations.ylt: who such a charge having received, did put them to the inner prison, and their feet made fast in the stocks.
translations.web: Having received such a command, he threw them into the inner prison and secured their feet in the stocks.

translations.kjv: And at midnight Paul and Silas prayed, and sang praises unto God: and the prisoners heard them.
translations.ylt: And at midnight Paul and Silas praying, were singing hymns to God, and the prisoners were hearing them,
translations.web: But about midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the prisoners were listening to them.

translations.kjv: And suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken: and immediately all the doors were opened, and every one’s bands were loosed.
translations.ylt: and suddenly a great earthquake came, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken, opened also presently were all the doors, and of all--the bands were loosed;
translations.web: Suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken; and immediately all the doors were opened, and everyone’s bonds were loosened.

translations.kjv: And the keeper of the prison awaking out of his sleep, and seeing the prison doors open, he drew out his sword, and would have killed himself, supposing that the prisoners had been fled.
translations.ylt: and the jailor having come out of sleep, and having seen the doors of the prison open, having drawn a sword, was about to kill himself, supposing the prisoners to be fled,
translations.web: The jailer, being roused out of sleep and seeing the prison doors open, drew his sword and was about to kill himself, supposing that the prisoners had escaped.

translations.kjv: But Paul cried with a loud voice, saying, Do thyself no harm: for we are all here.
translations.ylt: and Paul cried out with a loud voice, saying, `Thou mayest not do thyself any harm, for we are all here.'
translations.web: But Paul cried with a loud voice, saying, “Don’t harm yourself, for we are all here!”

translations.kjv: Then he called for a light, and sprang in, and came trembling, and fell down before Paul and Silas,
translations.ylt: And, having asked for a light, he sprang in, and trembling he fell down before Paul and Silas,
translations.web: He called for lights, sprang in, fell down trembling before Paul and Silas,

translations.kjv: And brought them out, and said, Sirs, what must I do to be saved?
translations.ylt: and having brought them forth, said, `Sirs, what must I do--that I may be saved?'
translations.web: brought them out, and said, “Sirs, what must I do to be saved?”

translations.kjv: And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, and thy house.
translations.ylt: and they said, `Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved--thou and thy house;'
translations.web: They said, “Believe in the Lord Jesus Christ, and you will be saved, you and your household.”

translations.kjv: And they spake unto him the word of the Lord, and to all that were in his house.
translations.ylt: and they spake to him the word of the Lord, and to all those in his household;
translations.web: They spoke the word of the Lord to him, and to all who were in his house.

translations.kjv: And he took them the same hour of the night, and washed their stripes; and was baptized, he and all his, straightway.
translations.ylt: and having taken them, in that hour of the night, he did bathe them from the blows, and was baptized, himself and all his presently,
translations.web: He took them the same hour of the night and washed their stripes, and was immediately baptized, he and all his household.

translations.kjv: And when he had brought them into his house, he set meat before them, and rejoiced, believing in God with all his house.
translations.ylt: having brought them also into his house, he set food before them, and was glad with all the household, he having believed in God.
translations.web: He brought them up into his house and set food before them, and rejoiced greatly with all his household, having believed in God.

translations.kjv: And when it was day, the magistrates sent the serjeants, saying, Let those men go.
translations.ylt: And day having come, the magistrates sent the rod-bearers, saying, `Let those men go;'
translations.web: But when it was day, the magistrates sent the sergeants, saying, “Let those men go.”

translations.kjv: And the keeper of the prison told this saying to Paul, The magistrates have sent to let you go: now therefore depart, and go in peace.
translations.ylt: and the jailor told these words unto Paul--`The magistrates have sent, that ye may be let go; now, therefore, having gone forth go on in peace;'
translations.web: The jailer reported these words to Paul, saying, “The magistrates have sent to let you go; now therefore come out and go in peace.”

translations.kjv: But Paul said unto them, They have beaten us openly uncondemned, being Romans, and have cast us into prison; and now do they thrust us out privily? nay verily; but let them come themselves and fetch us out.
translations.ylt: and Paul said to them, `Having beaten us publicly uncondemned--men, Romans being--they did cast us to prison, and now privately do they cast us forth! why no! but having come themselves, let them bring us forth.'
translations.web: But Paul said to them, “They have beaten us publicly without a trial, men who are Romans, and have cast us into prison! Do they now release us secretly? No, most certainly, but let them come themselves and bring us out!”

translations.kjv: And the serjeants told these words unto the magistrates: and they feared, when they heard that they were Romans.
translations.ylt: And the rod-bearers told to the magistrates these sayings, and they were afraid, having heard that they are Romans,
translations.web: The sergeants reported these words to the magistrates, and they were afraid when they heard that they were Romans,

translations.kjv: And they came and besought them, and brought them out, and desired them to depart out of the city.
translations.ylt: and having come, they besought them, and having brought them forth, they were asking them to go forth from the city;
translations.web: and they came and begged them. When they had brought them out, they asked them to depart from the city.

translations.kjv: And they went out of the prison, and entered into the house of Lydia: and when they had seen the brethren, they comforted them, and departed.
translations.ylt: and they, having gone forth out of the prison, entered into the house of Lydia, and having seen the brethren, they comforted them, and went forth.
translations.web: They went out of the prison and entered into Lydia’s house. When they had seen the brothers, they encouraged them, then departed.

translations.kjv: Now when they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where was a synagogue of the Jews:
translations.ylt: And having passed through Amphipolis, and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where was the synagogue of the Jews,
translations.web: Now when they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where there was a Jewish synagogue.

translations.kjv: And Paul, as his manner was, went in unto them, and three sabbath days reasoned with them out of the scriptures,
translations.ylt: and according to the custom of Paul, he went in unto them, and for three sabbaths he was reasoning with them from the Writings,
translations.web: Paul, as was his custom, went in to them; and for three Sabbath days reasoned with them from the Scriptures,

translations.kjv: Opening and alleging, that Christ must needs have suffered, and risen again from the dead; and that this Jesus, whom I preach unto you, is Christ.
translations.ylt: opening and alleging, `That the Christ it behoved to suffer, and to rise again out of the dead, and that this is the Christ--Jesus whom I proclaim to you.'
translations.web: explaining and demonstrating that the Christ had to suffer and rise again from the dead, and saying, “This Jesus, whom I proclaim to you, is the Christ.”

translations.kjv: And some of them believed, and consorted with Paul and Silas; and of the devout Greeks a great multitude, and of the chief women not a few.
translations.ylt: And certain of them did believe, and attached themselves to Paul and to Silas, also of the worshipping Greeks a great multitude, of the principal women also not a few.
translations.web: Some of them were persuaded and joined Paul and Silas: of the devout Greeks a great multitude, and not a few of the chief women.

translations.kjv: But the Jews which believed not, moved with envy, took unto them certain lewd fellows of the baser sort, and gathered a company, and set all the city on an uproar, and assaulted the house of Jason, and sought to bring them out to the people.
translations.ylt: And the unbelieving Jews, having been moved with envy, and having taken to them of the loungers certain evil men, and having made a crowd, were setting the city in an uproar; having assailed also the house of Jason, they were seeking them to bring them to the populace,
translations.web: But the unpersuaded Jews took along some wicked men from the marketplace and gathering a crowd, set the city in an uproar. Assaulting the house of Jason, they sought to bring them out to the people.

translations.kjv: And when they found them not, they drew Jason and certain brethren unto the rulers of the city, crying, These that have turned the world upside down are come hither also;
translations.ylt: and not having found them, they drew Jason and certain brethren unto the city rulers, calling aloud--`These, having put the world in commotion, are also here present,
translations.web: When they didn’t find them, they dragged Jason and certain brothers before the rulers of the city, crying, “These who have turned the world upside down have come here also,

translations.kjv: Whom Jason hath received: and these all do contrary to the decrees of Cesar, saying that there is another king, one Jesus.
translations.ylt: whom Jason hath received; and these all do contrary to the decrees of Caesar, saying another to be king--Jesus.'
translations.web: whom Jason has received. These all act contrary to the decrees of Caesar, saying that there is another king, Jesus!”

translations.kjv: And they troubled the people and the rulers of the city, when they heard these things.
translations.ylt: And they troubled the multitude and the city rulers, hearing these things,
translations.web: The multitude and the rulers of the city were troubled when they heard these things.

translations.kjv: And when they had taken security of Jason, and of the other, they let them go.
translations.ylt: and having taking security from Jason and the rest, they let them go.
translations.web: When they had taken security from Jason and the rest, they let them go.

translations.kjv: And the brethren immediately sent away Paul and Silas by night unto Berea: who coming thither went into the synagogue of the Jews.
translations.ylt: And the brethren immediately, through the night, sent forth both Paul and Silas to Berea, who having come, went to the synagogue of the Jews;
translations.web: The brothers immediately sent Paul and Silas away by night to Beroea. When they arrived, they went into the Jewish synagogue.

translations.kjv: These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.
translations.ylt: and these were more noble than those in Thessalonica, they received the word with all readiness of mind, every day examining the Writings whether those things were so;
translations.web: Now these were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, examining the Scriptures daily to see whether these things were so.

translations.kjv: Therefore many of them believed; also of honourable women which were Greeks, and of men, not a few.
translations.ylt: many, indeed, therefore, of them did believe, and of the honourable Greek women and men not a few.
translations.web: Many of them therefore believed; also of the prominent Greek women, and not a few men.

translations.kjv: But when the Jews of Thessalonica had knowledge that the word of God was preached of Paul at Berea, they came thither also, and stirred up the people.
translations.ylt: And when the Jews from Thessalonica knew that also in Berea was the word of God declared by Paul, they came thither also, agitating the multitudes;
translations.web: But when the Jews of Thessalonica had knowledge that the word of God was proclaimed by Paul at Beroea also, they came there likewise, agitating the multitudes.

translations.kjv: And then immediately the brethren sent away Paul to go as it were to the sea: but Silas and Timotheus abode there still.
translations.ylt: and then immediately the brethren sent forth Paul, to go on as it were to the sea, but both Silas and Timothy were remaining there.
translations.web: Then the brothers immediately sent out Paul to go as far as to the sea, and Silas and Timothy still stayed there.

translations.kjv: And they that conducted Paul brought him unto Athens: and receiving a commandment unto Silas and Timotheus for to come to him with all speed, they departed.
translations.ylt: And those conducting Paul, brought him unto Athens, and having received a command unto Silas and Timotheus that with all speed they may come unto him, they departed;
translations.web: But those who escorted Paul brought him as far as Athens. Receiving a commandment to Silas and Timothy that they should come to him very quickly, they departed.

translations.kjv: Now while Paul waited for them at Athens, his spirit was stirred in him, when he saw the city wholly given to idolatry.
translations.ylt: and Paul waiting for them in Athens, his spirit was stirred in him, beholding the city wholly given to idolatry,
translations.web: Now while Paul waited for them at Athens, his spirit was provoked within him as he saw the city full of idols.

translations.kjv: Therefore disputed he in the synagogue with the Jews, and with the devout persons, and in the market daily with them that met with him.
translations.ylt: therefore, indeed, he was reasoning in the synagogue with the Jews, and with the worshipping persons, and in the market-place every day with those who met with him.
translations.web: So he reasoned in the synagogue with the Jews and the devout persons, and in the marketplace every day with those who met him.

translations.kjv: Then certain philosophers of the Epicureans, and of the Stoicks, encountered him. And some said, What will this babbler say? other some, He seemeth to be a setter forth of strange gods: because he preached unto them Jesus, and the resurrection.
translations.ylt: And certain of the Epicurean and of the Stoic philosophers, were meeting together to see him, and some were saying, `What would this seed picker wish to say?' and others, `Of strange demons he doth seem to be an announcer;' because Jesus and the rising again he did proclaim to them as good news,
translations.web: Some of the Epicurean and Stoic philosophers also were conversing with him. Some said, “What does this babbler want to say?” Others said, “He seems to be advocating foreign deities,” because he preached Jesus and the resurrection.

translations.kjv: And they took him, and brought him unto Areopagus, saying, May we know what this new doctrine, whereof thou speakest, is?
translations.ylt: having also taken him, unto the Areopagus they brought him, saying, `Are we able to know what is this new teaching that is spoken by thee,
translations.web: They took hold of him and brought him to the Areopagus, saying, “May we know what this new teaching is, which you are speaking about?

translations.kjv: For thou bringest certain strange things to our ears: we would know therefore what these things mean.
translations.ylt: for certain strange things thou dost bring to our ears? we wish, then, to know what these things would wish to be;'
translations.web: For you bring certain strange things to our ears. We want to know therefore what these things mean.”

translations.kjv: (For all the Athenians and strangers which were there spent their time in nothing else, but either to tell, or to hear some new thing.)
translations.ylt: and all Athenians, and the strangers sojourning, for nothing else were at leisure but to say something, and to hear some newer thing.
translations.web: Now all the Athenians and the strangers living there spent their time in nothing else, but either to tell or to hear some new thing.

translations.kjv: Then Paul stood in the midst of Mars’ hill, and said, Ye men of Athens, I perceive that in all things ye are too superstitious.
translations.ylt: And Paul, having stood in the midst of the Areopagus, said, `Men, Athenians, in all things I perceive you as over-religious;
translations.web: Paul stood in the middle of the Areopagus and said, “You men of Athens, I perceive that you are very religious in all things.

translations.kjv: For as I passed by, and beheld your devotions, I found an altar with this inscription, TO THE UNKNOWN GOD. Whom therefore ye ignorantly worship, him declare I unto you.
translations.ylt: for passing through and contemplating your objects of worship, I found also an erection on which had been inscribed: To God--unknown; whom, therefore--not knowing--ye do worship, this One I announce to you.
translations.web: For as I passed along and observed the objects of your worship, I also found an altar with this inscription: ‘TO AN UNKNOWN GOD.’ What therefore you worship in ignorance, I announce to you.

translations.kjv: God that made the world and all things therein, seeing that he is Lord of heaven and earth, dwelleth not in temples made with hands;
translations.ylt: `God, who did make the world, and all things in it, this One, of heaven and of earth being Lord, in temples made with hands doth not dwell,
translations.web: The God who made the world and all things in it, he, being Lord of heaven and earth, doesn’t dwell in temples made with hands.

translations.kjv: Neither is worshipped with men’s hands, as though he needed any thing, seeing he giveth to all life, and breath, and all things;
translations.ylt: neither by the hands of men is He served--needing anything, He giving to all life, and breath, and all things;
translations.web: He isn’t served by men’s hands, as though he needed anything, seeing he himself gives to all life and breath and all things.

translations.kjv: And hath made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth, and hath determined the times before appointed, and the bounds of their habitation;
translations.ylt: He made also of one blood every nation of men, to dwell upon all the face of the earth--having ordained times before appointed, and the bounds of their dwellings--
translations.web: He made from one blood every nation of men to dwell on all the surface of the earth, having determined appointed seasons and the boundaries of their dwellings,

translations.kjv: That they should seek the Lord, if haply they might feel after him, and find him, though he be not far from every one of us:
translations.ylt: to seek the Lord, if perhaps they did feel after Him and find, --though, indeed, He is not far from each one of us,
translations.web: that they should seek the Lord, if perhaps they might reach out for him and find him, though he is not far from each one of us.

translations.kjv: For in him we live, and move, and have our being; as certain also of your own poets have said, For we are also his offspring.
translations.ylt: for in Him we live, and move, and are; as also certain of your poets have said: For of Him also we are offspring.
translations.web: ‘For in him we live, move, and have our being.’ As some of your own poets have said, ‘For we are also his offspring.’

translations.kjv: Forasmuch then as we are the offspring of God, we ought not to think that the Godhead is like unto gold, or silver, or stone, graven by art and man’s device.
translations.ylt: `Being, therefore, offspring of God, we ought not to think the Godhead to be like to gold, or silver, or stone, graving of art and device of man;
translations.web: Being then the offspring of God, we ought not to think that the Divine Nature is like gold, or silver, or stone, engraved by art and design of man.

translations.kjv: And the times of this ignorance God winked at; but now commandeth all men every where to repent:
translations.ylt: the times, indeed, therefore, of the ignorance God having overlooked, doth now command all men everywhere to reform,
translations.web: The times of ignorance therefore God overlooked. But now he commands that all people everywhere should repent,

translations.kjv: Because he hath appointed a day, in the which he will judge the world in righteousness by that man whom he hath ordained; whereof he hath given assurance unto all men, in that he hath raised him from the dead.
translations.ylt: because He did set a day in which He is about to judge the world in righteousness, by a man whom He did ordain, having given assurance to all, having raised him out of the dead.'
translations.web: because he has appointed a day in which he will judge the world in righteousness by the man whom he has ordained; of which he has given assurance to all men, in that he has raised him from the dead.”

translations.kjv: And when they heard of the resurrection of the dead, some mocked: and others said, We will hear thee again of this matter.
translations.ylt: And having heard of a rising again of the dead, some, indeed, were mocking, but others said, `We will hear thee again concerning this;'
translations.web: Now when they heard of the resurrection of the dead, some mocked; but others said, “We want to hear you again concerning this.”

translations.kjv: So Paul departed from among them.
translations.ylt: and so Paul went forth from the midst of them,
translations.web: Thus Paul went out from among them.

translations.kjv: Howbeit certain men clave unto him, and believed: among the which was Dionysius the Areopagite, and a woman named Damaris, and others with them.
translations.ylt: and certain men having cleaved to him, did believe, among whom is also Dionysius the Areopagite, and a woman, by name Damaris, and others with them.
translations.web: But certain men joined with him and believed, including Dionysius the Areopagite, and a woman named Damaris, and others with them.

translations.kjv: After these things Paul departed from Athens, and came to Corinth;
translations.ylt: And after these things, Paul having departed out of Athens, came to Corinth,
translations.web: After these things Paul departed from Athens and came to Corinth.

translations.kjv: And found a certain Jew named Aquila, born in Pontus, lately come from Italy, with his wife Priscilla; (because that Claudius had commanded all Jews to depart from Rome:) and came unto them.
translations.ylt: and having found a certain Jew, by name Aquilas, of Pontus by birth, lately come from Italy, and Priscilla his wife--because of Claudius having directed all the Jews to depart out of Rome--he came to them,
translations.web: He found a certain Jew named Aquila, a man of Pontus by race, who had recently come from Italy with his wife Priscilla, because Claudius had commanded all the Jews to depart from Rome. He came to them,

translations.kjv: And because he was of the same craft, he abode with them, and wrought: for by their occupation they were tentmakers.
translations.ylt: and because of being of the same craft, he did remain with them, and was working, for they were tent-makers as to craft;
translations.web: and because he practiced the same trade, he lived with them and worked, for by trade they were tent makers.

translations.kjv: And he reasoned in the synagogue every sabbath, and persuaded the Jews and the Greeks.
translations.ylt: and he was reasoning in the synagogue every sabbath, persuading both Jews and Greeks.
translations.web: He reasoned in the synagogue every Sabbath and persuaded Jews and Greeks.

translations.kjv: And when Silas and Timotheus were come from Macedonia, Paul was pressed in the spirit, and testified to the Jews that Jesus was Christ.
translations.ylt: And when both Silas and Timotheus came down from Macedonia, Paul was pressed in the Spirit, testifying fully to the Jews Jesus the Christ;
translations.web: When Silas and Timothy came down from Macedonia, Paul was compelled by the Spirit, testifying to the Jews that Jesus was the Christ.

translations.kjv: And when they opposed themselves, and blasphemed, he shook his raiment, and said unto them, Your blood be upon your own heads; I am clean: from henceforth I will go unto the Gentiles.
translations.ylt: and on their resisting and speaking evil, having shaken his garments, he said unto them, `Your blood is upon your head--I am clean; henceforth to the nations I will go on.'
translations.web: When they opposed him and blasphemed, he shook out his clothing and said to them, “Your blood be on your own heads! I am clean. From now on, I will go to the Gentiles!”

translations.kjv: And he departed thence, and entered into a certain man’s house, named Justus, one that worshipped God, whose house joined hard to the synagogue.
translations.ylt: And having departed thence, he went to the house of a certain one, by name Justus, a worshipper of God, whose house was adjoining the synagogue,
translations.web: He departed there and went into the house of a certain man named Justus, one who worshiped God, whose house was next door to the synagogue.

translations.kjv: And Crispus, the chief ruler of the synagogue, believed on the Lord with all his house; and many of the Corinthians hearing believed, and were baptized.
translations.ylt: and Crispus, the ruler of the synagogue did believe in the Lord with all his house, and many of the Corinthians hearing were believing, and they were being baptized.
translations.web: Crispus, the ruler of the synagogue, believed in the Lord with all his house. Many of the Corinthians, when they heard, believed and were baptized.

translations.kjv: Then spake the Lord to Paul in the night by a vision, Be not afraid, but speak, and hold not thy peace:
translations.ylt: And the Lord said through a vision in the night to Paul, `Be not afraid, but be speaking and thou mayest be not silent;
translations.web: The Lord said to Paul in the night by a vision, “Don’t be afraid, but speak and don’t be silent;

translations.kjv: For I am with thee, and no man shall set on thee to hurt thee: for I have much people in this city.
translations.ylt: because I am with thee, and no one shall set on thee to do thee evil; because I have much people in this city;'
translations.web: for I am with you, and no one will attack you to harm you, for I have many people in this city.”

translations.kjv: And he continued there a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them.
translations.ylt: and he continued a year and six months, teaching among them the word of God.
translations.web: He lived there a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them.

translations.kjv: And when Gallio was the deputy of Achaia, the Jews made insurrection with one accord against Paul, and brought him to the judgment seat,
translations.ylt: And Gallio being proconsul of Achaia, the Jews made a rush with one accord upon Paul, and brought him unto the tribunal,
translations.web: But when Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews with one accord rose up against Paul and brought him before the judgment seat,

translations.kjv: Saying, This fellow persuadeth men to worship God contrary to the law.
translations.ylt: saying--`Against the law this one doth persuade men to worship God;'
translations.web: saying, “This man persuades men to worship God contrary to the law.”

translations.kjv: And when Paul was now about to open his mouth, Gallio said unto the Jews, If it were a matter of wrong or wicked lewdness, O ye Jews, reason would that I should bear with you:
translations.ylt: and Paul being about to open his mouth, Gallio said unto the Jews, `If, indeed, then, it was anything unrighteous, or an act of wicked profligacy, O Jews, according to reason I had borne with you,
translations.web: But when Paul was about to open his mouth, Gallio said to the Jews, “If indeed it were a matter of wrong or of wicked crime, you Jews, it would be reasonable that I should bear with you;

translations.kjv: But if it be a question of words and names, and of your law, look ye to it; for I will be no judge of such matters.
translations.ylt: but if it is a question concerning words and names, and of your law, look ye yourselves to it, for a judge of these things I do not wish to be,'
translations.web: but if they are questions about words and names and your own law, look to it yourselves. For I don’t want to be a judge of these matters.”

translations.kjv: And he drave them from the judgment seat.
translations.ylt: and he drave them from the tribunal;
translations.web: So he drove them from the judgment seat.

translations.kjv: Then all the Greeks took Sosthenes, the chief ruler of the synagogue, and beat him before the judgment seat. And Gallio cared for none of those things.
translations.ylt: and all the Greeks having taken Sosthenes, the chief man of the synagogue, were beating him before the tribunal, and not even for these things was Gallio caring.
translations.web: Then all the Greeks seized Sosthenes, the ruler of the synagogue, and beat him before the judgment seat. Gallio didn’t care about any of these things.

translations.kjv: And Paul after this tarried there yet a good while, and then took his leave of the brethren, and sailed thence into Syria, and with him Priscilla and Aquila; having shorn his head in Cenchrea: for he had a vow.
translations.ylt: And Paul having remained yet a good many days, having taken leave of the brethren, was sailing to Syria--and with him are Priscilla and Aquilas--having shorn his head in Cenchera, for he had a vow;
translations.web: Paul, having stayed after this many more days, took his leave of the brothers, and sailed from there for Syria, together with Priscilla and Aquila. He shaved his head in Cenchreae, for he had a vow.

translations.kjv: And he came to Ephesus, and left them there: but he himself entered into the synagogue, and reasoned with the Jews.
translations.ylt: and he came down to Ephesus, and did leave them there, and he himself having entered into the synagogue did reason with the Jews:
translations.web: He came to Ephesus, and he left them there; but he himself entered into the synagogue and reasoned with the Jews.

translations.kjv: When they desired him to tarry longer time with them, he consented not;
translations.ylt: and they having requested him to remain a longer time with them, he did not consent,
translations.web: When they asked him to stay with them a longer time, he declined;

translations.kjv: But bade them farewell, saying, I must by all means keep this feast that cometh in Jerusalem: but I will return again unto you, if God will. And he sailed from Ephesus.
translations.ylt: but took leave of them, saying, `It behoveth me by all means the coming feast to keep at Jerusalem, and again I will return unto you--God willing.' And he sailed from Ephesus,
translations.web: but taking his leave of them, he said, “I must by all means keep this coming feast in Jerusalem, but I will return again to you if God wills.” Then he set sail from Ephesus.

translations.kjv: And when he had landed at Cesarea, and gone up, and saluted the church, he went down to Antioch.
translations.ylt: and having come down to Caesarea, having gone up, and having saluted the assembly, he went down to Antioch.
translations.web: When he had landed at Caesarea, he went up and greeted the assembly, and went down to Antioch.

translations.kjv: And after he had spent some time there, he departed, and went over all the country of Galatia and Phrygia in order, strengthening all the disciples.
translations.ylt: And having made some stay he went forth, going through in order the region of Galatia and Phrygia, strengthening all the disciples.
translations.web: Having spent some time there, he departed and went through the region of Galatia and Phrygia, in order, establishing all the disciples.

translations.kjv: And a certain Jew named Apollos, born at Alexandria, an eloquent man, and mighty in the scriptures, came to Ephesus.
translations.ylt: And a certain Jew, Apollos by name, an Alexandrian by birth, a man of eloquence, being mighty in the Writings, came to Ephesus,
translations.web: Now a certain Jew named Apollos, an Alexandrian by race, an eloquent man, came to Ephesus. He was mighty in the Scriptures.

translations.kjv: This man was instructed in the way of the Lord; and being fervent in the spirit, he spake and taught diligently the things of the Lord, knowing only the baptism of John.
translations.ylt: this one was instructed in the way of the Lord, and being fervent in the Spirit, was speaking and teaching exactly the things about the Lord, knowing only the baptism of John;
translations.web: This man had been instructed in the way of the Lord; and being fervent in spirit, he spoke and taught accurately the things concerning Jesus, although he knew only the baptism of John.

translations.kjv: And he began to speak boldly in the synagogue: whom when Aquila and Priscilla had heard, they took him unto them, and expounded unto him the way of God more perfectly.
translations.ylt: this one also began to speak boldly in the synagogue, and Aquilas and Priscilla having heard of him, took him to them, and did more exactly expound to him the way of God,
translations.web: He began to speak boldly in the synagogue. But when Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him aside, and explained to him the way of God more accurately.

translations.kjv: And when he was disposed to pass into Achaia, the brethren wrote, exhorting the disciples to receive him: who, when he was come, helped them much which had believed through grace:
translations.ylt: and he being minded to go through into Achaia, the brethren wrote to the disciples, having exhorted them to receive him, who having come, did help them much who have believed through the grace,
translations.web: When he had determined to pass over into Achaia, the brothers encouraged him; and wrote to the disciples to receive him. When he had come, he greatly helped those who had believed through grace;

translations.kjv: For he mightily convinced the Jews, and that publickly, shewing by the scriptures that Jesus was Christ.
translations.ylt: for powerfully the Jews he was refuting publicly, shewing through the Writings Jesus to be the Christ.
translations.web: for he powerfully refuted the Jews, publicly showing by the Scriptures that Jesus was the Christ.

translations.kjv: And it came to pass, that, while Apollos was at Corinth, Paul having passed through the upper coasts came to Ephesus: and finding certain disciples,
translations.ylt: And it came to pass, in Apollos' being in Corinth, Paul having gone through the upper parts, came to Ephesus, and having found certain disciples,
translations.web: While Apollos was at Corinth, Paul, having passed through the upper country, came to Ephesus and found certain disciples.

translations.kjv: He said unto them, Have ye received the Holy Ghost since ye believed? And they said unto him, We have not so much as heard whether there be any Holy Ghost.
translations.ylt: he said unto them, `The Holy Spirit did ye receive--having believed?' and they said unto him, `But we did not even hear whether there is any Holy Spirit;'
translations.web: He said to them, “Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you believed?” They said to him, “No, we haven’t even heard that there is a Holy Spirit.”

translations.kjv: And he said unto them, Unto what then were ye baptized? And they said, Unto John’s baptism.
translations.ylt: and he said unto them, `To what, then, were ye baptized?' and they said, `To John's baptism.'
translations.web: He said, “Into what then were you baptized?” They said, “Into John’s baptism.”

translations.kjv: Then said Paul, John verily baptized with the baptism of repentance, saying unto the people, that they should believe on him which should come after him, that is, on Christ Jesus.
translations.ylt: And Paul said, `John, indeed, did baptize with a baptism of reformation, saying to the people that in him who is coming after him they should believe--that is, in the Christ--Jesus;'
translations.web: Paul said, “John indeed baptized with the baptism of repentance, saying to the people that they should believe in the one who would come after him, that is, in Christ Jesus.”

translations.kjv: When they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
translations.ylt: and they, having heard, were baptized--to the name of the Lord Jesus,
translations.web: When they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.

translations.kjv: And when Paul had laid his hands upon them, the Holy Ghost came on them; and they spake with tongues, and prophesied.
translations.ylt: and Paul having laid on them his hands, the Holy Spirit came upon them, they were speaking also with tongues, and prophesying,
translations.web: When Paul had laid his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came on them and they spoke with other languages and prophesied.

translations.kjv: And all the men were about twelve.
translations.ylt: and all the men were, as it were, twelve.
translations.web: They were about twelve men in all.

translations.kjv: And he went into the synagogue, and spake boldly for the space of three months, disputing and persuading the things concerning the kingdom of God.
translations.ylt: And having gone into the synagogue, he was speaking boldly for three months, reasoning and persuading the things concerning the reign of God,
translations.web: He entered into the synagogue and spoke boldly for a period of three months, reasoning and persuading about the things concerning God’s Kingdom.

translations.kjv: But when divers were hardened, and believed not, but spake evil of that way before the multitude, he departed from them, and separated the disciples, disputing daily in the school of one Tyrannus.
translations.ylt: and when certain were hardened and were disbelieving, speaking evil of the way before the multitude, having departed from them, he did separate the disciples, every day reasoning in the school of a certain Tyrannus.
translations.web: But when some were hardened and disobedient, speaking evil of the Way before the multitude, he departed from them and separated the disciples, reasoning daily in the school of Tyrannus.

translations.kjv: And this continued by the space of two years; so that all they which dwelt in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks.
translations.ylt: And this happened for two years so that all those dwelling in Asia did hear the word of the Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks,
translations.web: This continued for two years, so that all those who lived in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks.

translations.kjv: And God wrought special miracles by the hands of Paul:
translations.ylt: mighty works also--not common--was God working through the hands of Paul,
translations.web: God worked special miracles by the hands of Paul,

translations.kjv: So that from his body were brought unto the sick handkerchiefs or aprons, and the diseases departed from them, and the evil spirits went out of them.
translations.ylt: so that even unto the ailing were brought from his body handkerchiefs or aprons, and the sicknesses departed from them; the evil spirits also went forth from them.
translations.web: so that even handkerchiefs or aprons were carried away from his body to the sick, and the diseases departed from them, and the evil spirits went out.

translations.kjv: Then certain of the vagabond Jews, exorcists, took upon them to call over them which had evil spirits the name of the Lord Jesus, saying, We adjure you by Jesus whom Paul preacheth.
translations.ylt: And certain of the wandering exorcist Jews, took upon them to name over those having the evil spirits the name of the Lord Jesus, saying, `We adjure you by Jesus, whom Paul doth preach;'
translations.web: But some of the itinerant Jews, exorcists, took on themselves to invoke over those who had the evil spirits the name of the Lord Jesus, saying, “We adjure you by Jesus whom Paul preaches.”

translations.kjv: And there were seven sons of one Sceva, a Jew, and chief of the priests, which did so.
translations.ylt: and there were certain--seven sons of Sceva, a Jew, a chief priest--who are doing this thing;
translations.web: There were seven sons of one Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, who did this.

translations.kjv: And the evil spirit answered and said, Jesus I know, and Paul I know; but who are ye?
translations.ylt: and the evil spirit, answering, said, `Jesus I know, and Paul I am acquainted with; and ye--who are ye?'
translations.web: The evil spirit answered, “Jesus I know, and Paul I know, but who are you?”

translations.kjv: And the man in whom the evil spirit was leaped on them, and overcame them, and prevailed against them, so that they fled out of that house naked and wounded.
translations.ylt: And the man, in whom was the evil spirit, leaping upon them, and having overcome them, prevailed against them, so that naked and wounded they did flee out of that house,
translations.web: The man in whom the evil spirit was leaped on them, overpowered them, and prevailed against them, so that they fled out of that house naked and wounded.

translations.kjv: And this was known to all the Jews and Greeks also dwelling at Ephesus; and fear fell on them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified.
translations.ylt: and this became known to all, both Jews and Greeks, who are dwelling at Ephesus, and fear fell upon them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was being magnified,
translations.web: This became known to all, both Jews and Greeks, who lived at Ephesus. Fear fell on them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified.

translations.kjv: And many that believed came, and confessed, and shewed their deeds.
translations.ylt: many also of those who did believe were coming, confessing and declaring their acts,
translations.web: Many also of those who had believed came, confessing and declaring their deeds.

translations.kjv: Many of them also which used curious arts brought their books together, and burned them before all men: and they counted the price of them, and found it fifty thousand pieces of silver.
translations.ylt: and many of those who had practised the curious arts, having brought the books together, were burning them before all; and they reckoned together the prices of them, and found it five myriads of silverlings;
translations.web: Many of those who practiced magical arts brought their books together and burned them in the sight of all. They counted their price, and found it to be fifty thousand pieces of silver.

translations.kjv: So mightily grew the word of God and prevailed.
translations.ylt: so powerfully was the word of God increasing and prevailing.
translations.web: So the word of the Lord was growing and becoming mighty.

translations.kjv: After these things were ended, Paul purposed in the spirit, when he had passed through Macedonia and Achaia, to go to Jerusalem, saying, After I have been there, I must also see Rome.
translations.ylt: And when these things were fulfilled, Paul purposed in the Spirit, having gone through Macedonia and Achaia, to go on to Jerusalem, saying--`After my being there, it behoveth me also to see Rome;'
translations.web: Now after these things had ended, Paul determined in the Spirit, when he had passed through Macedonia and Achaia, to go to Jerusalem, saying, “After I have been there, I must also see Rome.”

translations.kjv: So he sent into Macedonia two of them that ministered unto him, Timotheus and Erastus; but he himself stayed in Asia for a season.
translations.ylt: and having sent to Macedonia two of those ministering to him--Timotheus and Erastus--he himself stayed a time in Asia.
translations.web: Having sent into Macedonia two of those who served him, Timothy and Erastus, he himself stayed in Asia for a while.

translations.kjv: And the same time there arose no small stir about that way.
translations.ylt: And there came, at that time, not a little stir about the way,
translations.web: About that time there arose no small disturbance concerning the Way.

translations.kjv: For a certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith, which made silver shrines for Diana, brought no small gain unto the craftsmen;
translations.ylt: for a certain one, Demetrius by name, a worker in silver, making silver sanctuaries of Artemis, was bringing to the artificers gain not a little,
translations.web: For a certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith who made silver shrines of Artemis, brought no little business to the craftsmen,

translations.kjv: Whom he called together with the workmen of like occupation, and said, Sirs, ye know that by this craft we have our wealth.
translations.ylt: whom, having brought in a crowd together, and those who did work about such things, he said, `Men, ye know that by this work we have our wealth;
translations.web: whom he gathered together with the workmen of like occupation, and said, “Sirs, you know that by this business we have our wealth.

translations.kjv: Moreover ye see and hear, that not alone at Ephesus, but almost throughout all Asia, this Paul hath persuaded and turned away much people, saying that they be no gods, which are made with hands:
translations.ylt: and ye see and hear, that not only at Ephesus, but almost in all Asia, this Paul, having persuaded, did turn away a great multitude, saying, that they are not gods who are made by hands;
translations.web: You see and hear that not at Ephesus alone, but almost throughout all Asia, this Paul has persuaded and turned away many people, saying that they are no gods that are made with hands.

translations.kjv: So that not only this our craft is in danger to be set at nought; but also that the temple of the great goddess Diana should be despised, and her magnificence should be destroyed, whom all Asia and the world worshippeth.
translations.ylt: and not only is this department in danger for us of coming into disregard, but also, that of the great goddess Artemis the temple is to be reckoned for nothing, and also her greatness is about to be brought down, whom all Asia and the world doth worship.'
translations.web: Not only is there danger that this our trade come into disrepute, but also that the temple of the great goddess Artemis will be counted as nothing and her majesty destroyed, whom all Asia and the world worships.”

translations.kjv: And when they heard these sayings, they were full of wrath, and cried out, saying, Great is Diana of the Ephesians.
translations.ylt: And they having heard, and having become full of wrath, were crying out, saying, `Great is the Artemis of the Ephesians!'
translations.web: When they heard this they were filled with anger, and cried out, saying, “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”

translations.kjv: And the whole city was filled with confusion: and having caught Gaius and Aristarchus, men of Macedonia, Paul’s companions in travel, they rushed with one accord into the theatre.
translations.ylt: and the whole city was filled with confusion, they rushed also with one accord into the theatre, having caught Gaius and Aristarchus, Macedonians, Paul's fellow-travellers.
translations.web: The whole city was filled with confusion, and they rushed with one accord into the theater, having seized Gaius and Aristarchus, men of Macedonia, Paul’s companions in travel.

translations.kjv: And when Paul would have entered in unto the people, the disciples suffered him not.
translations.ylt: And on Paul's purposing to enter in unto the populace, the disciples were not suffering him,
translations.web: When Paul wanted to enter in to the people, the disciples didn’t allow him.

translations.kjv: And certain of the chief of Asia, which were his friends, sent unto him, desiring him that he would not adventure himself into the theatre.
translations.ylt: and certain also of the chief men of Asia, being his friends, having sent unto him, were entreating him not to venture himself into the theatre.
translations.web: Certain also of the Asiarchs, being his friends, sent to him and begged him not to venture into the theater.

translations.kjv: Some therefore cried one thing, and some another: for the assembly was confused; and the more part knew not wherefore they were come together.
translations.ylt: Some indeed, therefore, were calling out one thing, and some another, for the assembly was confused, and the greater part did not know for what they were come together;
translations.web: Some therefore cried one thing, and some another, for the assembly was in confusion. Most of them didn’t know why they had come together.

translations.kjv: And they drew Alexander out of the multitude, the Jews putting him forward. And Alexander beckoned with the hand, and would have made his defence unto the people.
translations.ylt: and out of the multitude they put forward Alexander--the Jews thrusting him forward--and Alexander having beckoned with the hand, wished to make defence to the populace,
translations.web: They brought Alexander out of the multitude, the Jews putting him forward. Alexander beckoned with his hand, and would have made a defense to the people.

translations.kjv: But when they knew that he was a Jew, all with one voice about the space of two hours cried out, Great is Diana of the Ephesians.
translations.ylt: and having known that he is a Jew, one voice came out of all, for about two hours, crying, `Great is the Artemis of the Ephesians!'
translations.web: But when they perceived that he was a Jew, all with one voice for a time of about two hours cried out, “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”

translations.kjv: And when the townclerk had appeased the people, he said, Ye men of Ephesus, what man is there that knoweth not how that the city of the Ephesians is a worshipper of the great goddess Diana, and of the image which fell down from Jupiter?
translations.ylt: And the public clerk having quieted the multitude, saith, `Men, Ephesians, why, who is the man that doth not know that the city of the Ephesians is a devotee of the great goddess Artemis, and of that which fell down from Zeus?
translations.web: When the town clerk had quieted the multitude, he said, “You men of Ephesus, what man is there who doesn’t know that the city of the Ephesians is temple keeper of the great goddess Artemis, and of the image which fell down from Zeus?

translations.kjv: Seeing then that these things cannot be spoken against, ye ought to be quiet, and to do nothing rashly.
translations.ylt: these things, then, not being to be gainsaid, it is necessary for you to be quiet, and to do nothing rashly.
translations.web: Seeing then that these things can’t be denied, you ought to be quiet and to do nothing rash.

translations.kjv: For ye have brought hither these men, which are neither robbers of churches, nor yet blasphemers of your goddess.
translations.ylt: `For ye brought these men, who are neither temple-robbers nor speaking evil of your goddess;
translations.web: For you have brought these men here, who are neither robbers of temples nor blasphemers of your goddess.

translations.kjv: Wherefore if Demetrius, and the craftsmen which are with him, have a matter against any man, the law is open, and there are deputies: let them implead one another.
translations.ylt: if indeed, therefore, Demetrius and the artificers with him with any one have a matter, court days are held, and there are proconsuls; let them accuse one another.
translations.web: If therefore Demetrius and the craftsmen who are with him have a matter against anyone, the courts are open and there are proconsuls. Let them press charges against one another.

translations.kjv: But if ye enquire any thing concerning other matters, it shall be determined in a lawful assembly.
translations.ylt: `And if ye seek after anything concerning other matters, in the legal assembly it shall be determined;
translations.web: But if you seek anything about other matters, it will be settled in the regular assembly.

translations.kjv: For we are in danger to be called in question for this day’s uproar, there being no cause whereby we may give an account of this concourse.
translations.ylt: for we are also in peril of being accused of insurrection in regard to this day, there being no occasion by which we shall be able to give an account of this concourse;'
translations.web: For indeed we are in danger of being accused concerning today’s riot, there being no cause. Concerning it, we wouldn’t be able to give an account of this commotion.”

translations.kjv: And after the uproar was ceased, Paul called unto him the disciples, and embraced them, and departed for to go into Macedonia.
translations.ylt: And after the ceasing of the tumult, Paul having called near the disciples, and having embraced them, went forth to go on to Macedonia;
translations.web: After the uproar had ceased, Paul sent for the disciples, took leave of them, and departed to go into Macedonia.

translations.kjv: And when he had gone over those parts, and had given them much exhortation, he came into Greece,
translations.ylt: and having gone through those parts, and having exhorted them with many words, he came to Greece;
translations.web: When he had gone through those parts and had encouraged them with many words, he came into Greece.

translations.kjv: And there abode three months. And when the Jews laid wait for him, as he was about to sail into Syria, he purposed to return through Macedonia.
translations.ylt: having made also three months' stay --a counsel of the Jews having been against him--being about to set forth to Syria, there came to him a resolution of returning through Macedonia.
translations.web: When he had spent three months there, and a plot was made against him by Jews as he was about to set sail for Syria, he determined to return through Macedonia.

translations.kjv: And there accompanied him into Asia Sopater of Berea; and of the Thessalonians, Aristarchus and Secundus; and Gaius of Derbe, and Timotheus; and of Asia, Tychicus and Trophimus.
translations.ylt: And there were accompanying him unto Asia, Sopater of Berea, and of Thessalonians Aristarchus and Secundus, and Gaius of Derbe, and Timotheus, and of Asiatics Tychicus and Trophimus;
translations.web: These accompanied him as far as Asia: Sopater of Beroea, Aristarchus and Secundus of the Thessalonians, Gaius of Derbe, Timothy, and Tychicus and Trophimus of Asia.

translations.kjv: These going before tarried for us at Troas.
translations.ylt: these, having gone before, did remain for us in Troas,
translations.web: But these had gone ahead, and were waiting for us at Troas.

translations.kjv: And we sailed away from Philippi after the days of unleavened bread, and came unto them to Troas in five days; where we abode seven days.
translations.ylt: and we sailed, after the days of the unleavened food, from Philippi, and came unto them to Troas in five days, where we abode seven days.
translations.web: We sailed away from Philippi after the days of Unleavened Bread, and came to them at Troas in five days, where we stayed seven days.

translations.kjv: And upon the first day of the week, when the disciples came together to break bread, Paul preached unto them, ready to depart on the morrow; and continued his speech until midnight.
translations.ylt: And on the first of the week, the disciples having been gathered together to break bread, Paul was discoursing to them, about to depart on the morrow, he was also continuing the discourse till midnight,
translations.web: On the first day of the week, when the disciples were gathered together to break bread, Paul talked with them, intending to depart on the next day; and continued his speech until midnight.

translations.kjv: And there were many lights in the upper chamber, where they were gathered together.
translations.ylt: and there were many lamps in the upper chamber where they were gathered together,
translations.web: There were many lights in the upper room where we were gathered together.

translations.kjv: And there sat in a window a certain young man named Eutychus, being fallen into a deep sleep: and as Paul was long preaching, he sunk down with sleep, and fell down from the third loft, and was taken up dead.
translations.ylt: and there was sitting a certain youth, by name Eutychus, upon the window--being borne down by a deep sleep, Paul discoursing long--he having sunk down from the sleep, fell down from the third story, and was lifted up dead.
translations.web: A certain young man named Eutychus sat in the window, weighed down with deep sleep. As Paul spoke still longer, being weighed down by his sleep, he fell down from the third floor and was taken up dead.

translations.kjv: And Paul went down, and fell on him, and embracing him said, Trouble not yourselves; for his life is in him.
translations.ylt: And Paul, having gone down, fell upon him, and having embraced him, said, `Make no tumult, for his life is in him;'
translations.web: Paul went down and fell upon him, and embracing him said, “Don’t be troubled, for his life is in him.”

translations.kjv: When he therefore was come up again, and had broken bread, and eaten, and talked a long while, even till break of day, so he departed.
translations.ylt: and having come up, and having broken bread, and having tasted, for a long time also having talked--till daylight, so he went forth,
translations.web: When he had gone up, had broken bread and eaten, and had talked with them a long while, even until break of day, he departed.

translations.kjv: And they brought the young man alive, and were not a little comforted.
translations.ylt: and they brought up the lad alive, and were comforted in no ordinary measure.
translations.web: They brought the boy in alive, and were greatly comforted.

translations.kjv: And we went before to ship, and sailed unto Assos, there intending to take in Paul: for so had he appointed, minding himself to go afoot.
translations.ylt: And we having gone before unto the ship, did sail to Assos, thence intending to take in Paul, for so he had arranged, intending himself to go on foot;
translations.web: But we, going ahead to the ship, set sail for Assos, intending to take Paul aboard there; for he had so arranged, intending himself to go by land.

translations.kjv: And when he met with us at Assos, we took him in, and came to Mitylene.
translations.ylt: and when he met with us at Assos, having taken him up, we came to Mitylene,
translations.web: When he met us at Assos, we took him aboard and came to Mitylene.

translations.kjv: And we sailed thence, and came the next day over against Chios; and the next day we arrived at Samos, and tarried at Trogyllium; and the next day we came to Miletus.
translations.ylt: and thence having sailed, on the morrow we came over-against Chios, and the next day we arrived at Samos, and having remained in Trogyllium, on the following day we came to Miletus,
translations.web: Sailing from there, we came the following day opposite Chios. The next day we touched at Samos and stayed at Trogyllium, and the day after we came to Miletus.

translations.kjv: For Paul had determined to sail by Ephesus, because he would not spend the time in Asia: for he hasted, if it were possible for him, to be at Jerusalem the day of Pentecost.
translations.ylt: for Paul decided to sail past Ephesus, that there may not be to him a loss of time in Asia, for he hasted, if it were possible for him, on the day of the Pentecost to be at Jerusalem.
translations.web: For Paul had determined to sail past Ephesus, that he might not have to spend time in Asia; for he was hastening, if it were possible for him, to be in Jerusalem on the day of Pentecost.

translations.kjv: And from Miletus he sent to Ephesus, and called the elders of the church.
translations.ylt: And from Miletus, having sent to Ephesus, he called for the elders of the assembly,
translations.web: From Miletus he sent to Ephesus and called to himself the elders of the assembly.

translations.kjv: And when they were come to him, he said unto them, Ye know, from the first day that I came into Asia, after what manner I have been with you at all seasons,
translations.ylt: and when they were come unto him, he said to them, `Ye--ye know from the first day in which I came to Asia, how, with you at all times I was;
translations.web: When they had come to him, he said to them, “You yourselves know, from the first day that I set foot in Asia, how I was with you all the time,

translations.kjv: Serving the Lord with all humility of mind, and with many tears, and temptations, which befell me by the lying in wait of the Jews:
translations.ylt: serving the Lord with all humility, and many tears, and temptations, that befell me in the counsels of the Jews against me;
translations.web: serving the Lord with all humility, with many tears, and with trials which happened to me by the plots of the Jews;

translations.kjv: And how I kept back nothing that was profitable unto you, but have shewed you, and have taught you publickly, and from house to house,
translations.ylt: how nothing I did keep back of what things are profitable, not to declare to you, and to teach you publicly, and in every house,
translations.web: how I didn’t shrink from declaring to you anything that was profitable, teaching you publicly and from house to house,

translations.kjv: Testifying both to the Jews, and also to the Greeks, repentance toward God, and faith toward our Lord Jesus Christ.
translations.ylt: testifying fully both to Jews and Greeks, toward God reformation, and faith toward our Lord Jesus Christ.
translations.web: testifying both to Jews and to Greeks repentance toward God and faith toward our Lord Jesus.

translations.kjv: And now, behold, I go bound in the spirit unto Jerusalem, not knowing the things that shall befall me there:
translations.ylt: `And now, lo, I--bound in the Spirit--go on to Jerusalem, the things that shall befall me in it not knowing,
translations.web: Now, behold, I go bound by the Spirit to Jerusalem, not knowing what will happen to me there;

translations.kjv: Save that the Holy Ghost witnesseth in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions abide me.
translations.ylt: save that the Holy Spirit in every city doth testify fully, saying, that for me bonds and tribulations remain;
translations.web: except that the Holy Spirit testifies in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions wait for me.

translations.kjv: But none of these things move me, neither count I my life dear unto myself, so that I might finish my course with joy, and the ministry, which I have received of the Lord Jesus, to testify the gospel of the grace of God.
translations.ylt: but I make account of none of these, neither do I count my life precious to myself, so that I finish my course with joy, and the ministration that I received from the Lord Jesus, to testify fully the good news of the grace of God.
translations.web: But these things don’t count; nor do I hold my life dear to myself, so that I may finish my race with joy, and the ministry which I received from the Lord Jesus, to fully testify to the Good News of the grace of God.

translations.kjv: And now, behold, I know that ye all, among whom I have gone preaching the kingdom of God, shall see my face no more.
translations.ylt: `And now, lo, I have known that no more shall ye see my face, --ye all among whom I did go preaching the reign of God;
translations.web: “Now, behold, I know that you all, among whom I went about preaching God’s Kingdom, will see my face no more.

translations.kjv: Wherefore I take you to record this day, that I am pure from the blood of all men.
translations.ylt: wherefore I take you to witness this day, that I am clear from the blood of all,
translations.web: Therefore I testify to you today that I am clean from the blood of all men,

translations.kjv: For I have not shunned to declare unto you all the counsel of God.
translations.ylt: for I did not keep back from declaring to you all the counsel of God.
translations.web: for I didn’t shrink from declaring to you the whole counsel of God.

translations.kjv: Take heed therefore unto yourselves, and to all the flock, over the which the Holy Ghost hath made you overseers, to feed the church of God, which he hath purchased with his own blood.
translations.ylt: `Take heed, therefore, to yourselves, and to all the flock, among which the Holy Spirit made you overseers, to feed the assembly of God that He acquired through His own blood,
translations.web: Take heed, therefore, to yourselves and to all the flock, in which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers, to shepherd the assembly of the Lord and God which he purchased with his own blood.

translations.kjv: For I know this, that after my departing shall grievous wolves enter in among you, not sparing the flock.
translations.ylt: for I have known this, that there shall enter in, after my departing, grievous wolves unto you, not sparing the flock,
translations.web: For I know that after my departure, vicious wolves will enter in among you, not sparing the flock.

translations.kjv: Also of your own selves shall men arise, speaking perverse things, to draw away disciples after them.
translations.ylt: and of your own selves there shall arise men, speaking perverse things, to draw away the disciples after them.
translations.web: Men will arise from among your own selves, speaking perverse things, to draw away the disciples after them.

translations.kjv: Therefore watch, and remember, that by the space of three years I ceased not to warn every one night and day with tears.
translations.ylt: `Therefore, watch, remembering that three years, night and day, I did not cease with tears warning each one;
translations.web: Therefore watch, remembering that for a period of three years I didn’t cease to admonish everyone night and day with tears.

translations.kjv: And now, brethren, I commend you to God, and to the word of his grace, which is able to build you up, and to give you an inheritance among all them which are sanctified.
translations.ylt: and now, I commend you, brethren, to God, and to the word of His grace, that is able to build up, and to give you an inheritance among all those sanctified.
translations.web: Now, brothers, I entrust you to God and to the word of his grace, which is able to build up and to give you the inheritance among all those who are sanctified.

translations.kjv: I have coveted no man’s silver, or gold, or apparel.
translations.ylt: `The silver or gold or garments of no one did I covet;
translations.web: I coveted no one’s silver, gold, or clothing.

translations.kjv: Yea, ye yourselves know, that these hands have ministered unto my necessities, and to them that were with me.
translations.ylt: and ye yourselves know that to my necessities, and to those who were with me, minister did these hands;
translations.web: You yourselves know that these hands served my necessities, and those who were with me.

translations.kjv: I have shewed you all things, how that so labouring ye ought to support the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, how he said, It is more blessed to give than to receive.
translations.ylt: all things I did shew you, that, thus labouring, it behoveth us to partake with the ailing, to be mindful also of the words of the Lord Jesus, that he himself said, It is more blessed to give than to receive.'
translations.web: In all things I gave you an example, that so laboring you ought to help the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, that he himself said, ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’ ”

translations.kjv: And when he had thus spoken, he kneeled down, and prayed with them all.
translations.ylt: And these things having said, having bowed his knees, with them all, he did pray,
translations.web: When he had spoken these things, he knelt down and prayed with them all.
