translations.kjv: And they all wept sore, and fell on Paul’s neck, and kissed him,
translations.ylt: and there came a great weeping to all, and having fallen upon the neck of Paul, they were kissing him,
translations.web: They all wept freely, and fell on Paul’s neck and kissed him,

translations.kjv: Sorrowing most of all for the words which he spake, that they should see his face no more. And they accompanied him unto the ship.
translations.ylt: sorrowing most of all for the word that he had said--that they are about no more to see his face; and they were accompanying him to the ship.
translations.web: sorrowing most of all because of the word which he had spoken, that they should see his face no more. Then they accompanied him to the ship.

translations.kjv: And it came to pass, that after we were gotten from them, and had launched, we came with a straight course unto Coos, and the day following unto Rhodes, and from thence unto Patara:
translations.ylt: And it came to pass, at our sailing, having been parted from them, having run direct, we came to Coos, and the succeeding day to Rhodes, and thence to Patara,
translations.web: When we had departed from them and had set sail, we came with a straight course to Cos, and the next day to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.

translations.kjv: And finding a ship sailing over unto Phenicia, we went aboard, and set forth.
translations.ylt: and having found a ship passing over to Phenicia, having gone on board, we sailed,
translations.web: Having found a ship crossing over to Phoenicia, we went aboard and set sail.

translations.kjv: Now when we had discovered Cyprus, we left it on the left hand, and sailed into Syria, and landed at Tyre: for there the ship was to unlade her burden.
translations.ylt: and having discovered Cyprus, and having left it on the left, we were sailing to Syria, and did land at Tyre, for there was the ship discharging the lading.
translations.web: When we had come in sight of Cyprus, leaving it on the left hand, we sailed to Syria and landed at Tyre, for the ship was there to unload her cargo.

translations.kjv: And finding disciples, we tarried there seven days: who said to Paul through the Spirit, that he should not go up to Jerusalem.
translations.ylt: And having found out the disciples, we tarried there seven days, and they said to Paul, through the Spirit, not to go up to Jerusalem;
translations.web: Having found disciples, we stayed there seven days. These said to Paul through the Spirit that he should not go up to Jerusalem.

translations.kjv: And when we had accomplished those days, we departed and went our way; and they all brought us on our way, with wives and children, till we were out of the city: and we kneeled down on the shore, and prayed.
translations.ylt: but when it came that we completed the days, having gone forth, we went on, all bringing us on the way, with women and children, unto the outside of the city, and having bowed the knees upon the shore, we prayed,
translations.web: When those days were over, we departed and went on our journey. They all, with wives and children, brought us on our way until we were out of the city. Kneeling down on the beach, we prayed.

translations.kjv: And when we had taken our leave one of another, we took ship; and they returned home again.
translations.ylt: and having embraced one another, we embarked in the ship, and they returned to their own friends.
translations.web: After saying goodbye to each other, we went on board the ship, and they returned home again.

translations.kjv: And when we had finished our course from Tyre, we came to Ptolemais, and saluted the brethren, and abode with them one day.
translations.ylt: And we, having finished the course, from Tyre came down to Ptolemais, and having saluted the brethren, we remained one day with them;
translations.web: When we had finished the voyage from Tyre, we arrived at Ptolemais. We greeted the brothers and stayed with them one day.

translations.kjv: And the next day we that were of Paul’s company departed, and came unto Cesarea: and we entered into the house of Philip the evangelist, which was one of the seven; and abode with him.
translations.ylt: and on the morrow Paul and his company having gone forth, we came to Caesarea, and having entered into the house of Philip the evangelist--who is of the seven--we remained with him,
translations.web: On the next day, we who were Paul’s companions departed and came to Caesarea. We entered into the house of Philip the evangelist, who was one of the seven, and stayed with him.

translations.kjv: And the same man had four daughters, virgins, which did prophesy.
translations.ylt: and this one had four daughters, virgins, prophesying.
translations.web: Now this man had four virgin daughters who prophesied.

translations.kjv: And as we tarried there many days, there came down from Judea a certain prophet, named Agabus.
translations.ylt: And we remaining many more days, there came down a certain one from Judea, a prophet, by name Agabus,
translations.web: As we stayed there some days, a certain prophet named Agabus came down from Judea.

translations.kjv: And when he was come unto us, he took Paul’s girdle, and bound his own hands and feet, and said, Thus saith the Holy Ghost, So shall the Jews at Jerusalem bind the man that owneth this girdle, and shall deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles.
translations.ylt: and he having come unto us, and having taken up the girdle of Paul, having bound also his own hands and feet, said, `Thus saith the Holy Spirit, The man whose is this girdle--so shall the Jews in Jerusalem bind, and they shall deliver him up to the hands of nations.'
translations.web: Coming to us and taking Paul’s belt, he bound his own feet and hands, and said, “The Holy Spirit says: ‘So the Jews at Jerusalem will bind the man who owns this belt, and will deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles.’”

translations.kjv: And when we heard these things, both we, and they of that place, besought him not to go up to Jerusalem.
translations.ylt: And when we heard these things, we called upon him --both we, and those of that place--not to go up to Jerusalem,
translations.web: When we heard these things, both we and the people of that place begged him not to go up to Jerusalem.

translations.kjv: Then Paul answered, What mean ye to weep and to break mine heart? for I am ready not to be bound only, but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.
translations.ylt: and Paul answered, `What do ye--weeping, and crushing mine heart? for I, not only to be bound, but also to die at Jerusalem, am ready, for the name of the Lord Jesus;'
translations.web: Then Paul answered, “What are you doing, weeping and breaking my heart? For I am ready not only to be bound, but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.”

translations.kjv: And when he would not be persuaded, we ceased, saying, The will of the Lord be done.
translations.ylt: and he not being persuaded, we were silent, saying, `The will of the Lord be done.'
translations.web: When he would not be persuaded, we ceased, saying, “The Lord’s will be done.”

translations.kjv: And after those days we took up our carriages, and went up to Jerusalem.
translations.ylt: And after these days, having taken our vessels, we were going up to Jerusalem,
translations.web: After these days we took up our baggage and went up to Jerusalem.

translations.kjv: There went with us also certain of the disciples of Cesarea, and brought with them one Mnason of Cyprus, an old disciple, with whom we should lodge.
translations.ylt: and there went also of the disciples from Caesarea with us, bringing with them him with whom we may lodge, a certain Mnason of Cyprus, an aged disciple.
translations.web: Some of the disciples from Caesarea also went with us, bringing one Mnason of Cyprus, an early disciple, with whom we would stay.

translations.kjv: And when we were come to Jerusalem, the brethren received us gladly.
translations.ylt: And we having come to Jerusalem, the brethren did gladly receive us,
translations.web: When we had come to Jerusalem, the brothers received us gladly.

translations.kjv: And the day following Paul went in with us unto James; and all the elders were present.
translations.ylt: and on the morrow Paul was going in with us unto James, all the elders also came,
translations.web: The day following, Paul went in with us to James; and all the elders were present.

translations.kjv: And when he had saluted them, he declared particularly what things God had wrought among the Gentiles by his ministry.
translations.ylt: and having saluted them, he was declaring, one by one, each of the things God did among the nations through his ministration,
translations.web: When he had greeted them, he reported one by one the things which God had worked among the Gentiles through his ministry.

translations.kjv: And when they heard it, they glorified the Lord, and said unto him, Thou seest, brother, how many thousands of Jews there are which believe; and they are all zealous of the law:
translations.ylt: and they having heard, were glorifying the Lord. They said also to him, `Thou seest, brother, how many myriads there are of Jews who have believed, and all are zealous of the law,
translations.web: They, when they heard it, glorified God. They said to him, “You see, brother, how many thousands there are among the Jews of those who have believed, and they are all zealous for the law.

translations.kjv: And they are informed of thee, that thou teachest all the Jews which are among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, saying that they ought not to circumcise their children, neither to walk after the customs.
translations.ylt: and they are instructed concerning thee, that apostasy from Moses thou dost teach to all Jews among the nations, saying--Not to circumcise the children, nor after the customs to walk;
translations.web: They have been informed about you, that you teach all the Jews who are among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, telling them not to circumcise their children and not to walk after the customs.

translations.kjv: What is it therefore? the multitude must needs come together: for they will hear that thou art come.
translations.ylt: what then is it? certainly the multitude it behoveth to come together, for they will hear that thou hast come.
translations.web: What then? The assembly must certainly meet, for they will hear that you have come.

translations.kjv: Do therefore this that we say to thee: We have four men which have a vow on them;
translations.ylt: `This, therefore, do that we say to thee: We have four men having a vow on themselves,
translations.web: Therefore do what we tell you. We have four men who have taken a vow.

translations.kjv: Them take, and purify thyself with them, and be at charges with them, that they may shave their heads: and all may know that those things, whereof they were informed concerning thee, are nothing; but that thou thyself also walkest orderly, and keepest the law.
translations.ylt: these having taken, be purified with them, and be at expence with them, that they may shave the head, and all may know that the things of which they have been instructed concerning thee are nothing, but thou dost walk--thyself also--the law keeping.
translations.web: Take them and purify yourself with them, and pay their expenses for them, that they may shave their heads. Then all will know that there is no truth in the things that they have been informed about you, but that you yourself also walk keeping the law.

translations.kjv: As touching the Gentiles which believe, we have written and concluded that they observe no such thing, save only that they keep themselves from things offered to idols, and from blood, and from strangled, and from fornication.
translations.ylt: `And concerning those of the nations who have believed, we have written, having given judgment, that they observe no such thing, except to keep themselves both from idol-sacrifices, and blood, and a strangled thing, and whoredom.'
translations.web: But concerning the Gentiles who believe, we have written our decision that they should observe no such thing, except that they should keep themselves from food offered to idols, from blood, from strangled things, and from sexual immorality.”

translations.kjv: Then Paul took the men, and the next day purifying himself with them entered into the temple, to signify the accomplishment of the days of purification, until that an offering should be offered for every one of them.
translations.ylt: Then Paul, having taken the men, on the following day, with them having purified himself, was entering into the temple, announcing the fulfilment of the days of the purification, till the offering was offered for each one of them.
translations.web: Then Paul took the men, and the next day purified himself and went with them into the temple, declaring the fulfillment of the days of purification, until the offering was offered for every one of them.

translations.kjv: And when the seven days were almost ended, the Jews which were of Asia, when they saw him in the temple, stirred up all the people, and laid hands on him,
translations.ylt: And, as the seven days were about to be fully ended, the Jews from Asia having beheld him in the temple, were stirring up all the multitude, and they laid hands upon him,
translations.web: When the seven days were almost completed, the Jews from Asia, when they saw him in the temple, stirred up all the multitude and laid hands on him,

translations.kjv: Crying out, Men of Israel, help: This is the man, that teacheth all men every where against the people, and the law, and this place: and further brought Greeks also into the temple, and hath polluted this holy place.
translations.ylt: crying out, `Men, Israelites, help! this is the man who, against the people, and the law, and this place, all everywhere is teaching; and further, also, Greeks he brought into the temple, and hath defiled this holy place;'
translations.web: crying out, “Men of Israel, help! This is the man who teaches all men everywhere against the people, and the law, and this place. Moreover, he also brought Greeks into the temple and has defiled this holy place!”

translations.kjv: (For they had seen before with him in the city Trophimus an Ephesian, whom they supposed that Paul had brought into the temple.)
translations.ylt: for they had seen before Trophimus, the Ephesian, in the city with him, whom they were supposing that Paul brought into the temple.
translations.web: For they had seen Trophimus the Ephesian with him in the city, and they supposed that Paul had brought him into the temple.

translations.kjv: And all the city was moved, and the people ran together: and they took Paul, and drew him out of the temple: and forthwith the doors were shut.
translations.ylt: All the city also was moved and there was a running together of the people, and having laid hold on Paul, they were drawing him out of the temple, and immediately were the doors shut,
translations.web: All the city was moved and the people ran together. They seized Paul and dragged him out of the temple. Immediately the doors were shut.

translations.kjv: And as they went about to kill him, tidings came unto the chief captain of the band, that all Jerusalem was in an uproar.
translations.ylt: and they seeking to kill him, a rumour came to the chief captain of the band that all Jerusalem hath been thrown into confusion,
translations.web: As they were trying to kill him, news came up to the commanding officer of the regiment that all Jerusalem was in an uproar.

translations.kjv: Who immediately took soldiers and centurions, and ran down unto them: and when they saw the chief captain and the soldiers, they left beating of Paul.
translations.ylt: who, at once, having taken soldiers and centurions, ran down upon them, and they having seen the chief captain and the soldiers, did leave off beating Paul.
translations.web: Immediately he took soldiers and centurions and ran down to them. They, when they saw the chief captain and the soldiers, stopped beating Paul.

translations.kjv: Then the chief captain came near, and took him, and commanded him to be bound with two chains; and demanded who he was, and what he had done.
translations.ylt: Then the chief captain, having come nigh, took him, and commanded him to be bound with two chains, and was inquiring who he may be, and what it is he hath been doing,
translations.web: Then the commanding officer came near, arrested him, commanded him to be bound with two chains, and inquired who he was and what he had done.

translations.kjv: And some cried one thing, some another, among the multitude: and when he could not know the certainty for the tumult, he commanded him to be carried into the castle.
translations.ylt: and some were crying out one thing, and some another, among the multitude, and not being able to know the certainty because of the tumult, he commanded him to be carried to the castle,
translations.web: Some shouted one thing and some another, among the crowd. When he couldn’t find out the truth because of the noise, he commanded him to be brought into the barracks.

translations.kjv: And when he came upon the stairs, so it was, that he was borne of the soldiers for the violence of the people.
translations.ylt: and when he came upon the steps, it happened he was borne by the soldiers, because of the violence of the multitude,
translations.web: When he came to the stairs, he was carried by the soldiers because of the violence of the crowd;

translations.kjv: For the multitude of the people followed after, crying, Away with him.
translations.ylt: for the crowd of the people was following after, crying, `Away with him.'
translations.web: for the multitude of the people followed after, crying out, “Away with him!”

translations.kjv: And as Paul was to be led into the castle, he said unto the chief captain, May I speak unto thee? Who said, Canst thou speak Greek?
translations.ylt: And Paul being about to be led into the castle, saith to the chief captain, `Is it permitted to me to say anything unto thee?' and he said, `Greek dost thou know?
translations.web: As Paul was about to be brought into the barracks, he asked the commanding officer, “May I speak to you?” He said, “Do you know Greek?

translations.kjv: Art not thou that Egyptian, which before these days madest an uproar, and leddest out into the wilderness four thousand men that were murderers?
translations.ylt: art not thou, then, the Egyptian who before these days made an uprising, and did lead into the desert the four thousand men of the assassins?'
translations.web: Aren’t you then the Egyptian who before these days stirred up to sedition and led out into the wilderness the four thousand men of the Assassins?”

translations.kjv: But Paul said, I am a man which am a Jew of Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, a citizen of no mean city: and, I beseech thee, suffer me to speak unto the people.
translations.ylt: And Paul said, `I, indeed, am a man, a Jew, of Tarsus of Cilicia, of no mean city a citizen; and I beseech thee, suffer me to speak unto the people.'
translations.web: But Paul said, “I am a Jew from Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no insignificant city. I beg you, allow me to speak to the people.”

translations.kjv: And when he had given him licence, Paul stood on the stairs, and beckoned with the hand unto the people. And when there was made a great silence, he spake unto them in the Hebrew tongue, saying,
translations.ylt: And he having given him leave, Paul having stood upon the stairs, did beckon with the hand to the people, and there having been a great silence, he spake unto them in the Hebrew dialect, saying:
translations.web: When he had given him permission, Paul, standing on the stairs, beckoned with his hand to the people. When there was a great silence, he spoke to them in the Hebrew language, saying,

translations.kjv: Men, brethren, and fathers, hear ye my defence which I make now unto you.
translations.ylt: `Men, brethren, and fathers, hear my defence now unto you;' --
translations.web: “Brothers and fathers, listen to the defense which I now make to you.”

translations.kjv: (And when they heard that he spake in the Hebrew tongue to them, they kept the more silence: and he saith,)
translations.ylt: and they having heard that in the Hebrew dialect he was speaking to them, gave the more silence, and he saith, --
translations.web: When they heard that he spoke to them in the Hebrew language, they were even more quiet. He said,

translations.kjv: I am verily a man which am a Jew, born in Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, yet brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, and taught according to the perfect manner of the law of the fathers, and was zealous toward God, as ye all are this day.
translations.ylt: `I, indeed, am a man, a Jew, having been born in Tarsus of Cilicia, and brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, having been taught according to the exactitude of a law of the fathers, being zealous of God, as all ye are to-day.
translations.web: “I am indeed a Jew, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, but brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, instructed according to the strict tradition of the law of our fathers, being zealous for God, even as you all are today.

translations.kjv: And I persecuted this way unto the death, binding and delivering into prisons both men and women.
translations.ylt: `And this way I persecuted unto death, binding and delivering up to prisons both men and women,
translations.web: I persecuted this Way to the death, binding and delivering into prisons both men and women,

translations.kjv: As also the high priest doth bear me witness, and all the estate of the elders: from whom also I received letters unto the brethren, and went to Damascus, to bring them which were there bound unto Jerusalem, for to be punished.
translations.ylt: as also the chief priest doth testify to me, and all the eldership; from whom also having received letters unto the brethren, to Damascus, I was going on, to bring also those there bound to Jerusalem that they might be punished,
translations.web: as also the high priest and all the council of the elders testify, from whom also I received letters to the brothers, and traveled to Damascus to bring them also who were there to Jerusalem in bonds to be punished.

translations.kjv: And it came to pass, that, as I made my journey, and was come nigh unto Damascus about noon, suddenly there shone from heaven a great light round about me.
translations.ylt: and it came to pass, in my going on and coming nigh to Damascus, about noon, suddenly out of the heaven there shone a great light round about me,
translations.web: “As I made my journey and came close to Damascus, about noon suddenly a great light shone around me from the sky.

translations.kjv: And I fell unto the ground, and heard a voice saying unto me, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?
translations.ylt: I fell also to the ground, and I heard a voice saying to me, Saul, Saul, why me dost thou persecute?
translations.web: I fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to me, ‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?’

translations.kjv: And I answered, Who art thou, Lord? And he said unto me, I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom thou persecutest.
translations.ylt: `And I answered, Who art thou, Lord? and he said unto me, I am Jesus the Nazarene whom thou dost persecute--
translations.web: I answered, ‘Who are you, Lord?’ He said to me, ‘I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom you persecute.’

translations.kjv: And they that were with me saw indeed the light, and were afraid; but they heard not the voice of him that spake to me.
translations.ylt: and they who are with me the light did see, and became afraid, and the voice they heard not of him who is speaking to me--
translations.web: “Those who were with me indeed saw the light and were afraid, but they didn’t understand the voice of him who spoke to me.

translations.kjv: And I said, What shall I do, Lord? And the Lord said unto me, Arise, and go into Damascus; and there it shall be told thee of all things which are appointed for thee to do.
translations.ylt: and I said, What shall I do, Lord? and the Lord said unto me, Having risen, go on to Damascus, and there it shall be told thee concerning all things that have been appointed for thee to do.
translations.web: I said, ‘What shall I do, Lord?’ The Lord said to me, ‘Arise, and go into Damascus. There you will be told about all things which are appointed for you to do.’

translations.kjv: And when I could not see for the glory of that light, being led by the hand of them that were with me, I came into Damascus.
translations.ylt: `And when I did not see from the glory of that light, being led by the hand by those who are with me, I came to Damascus,
translations.web: When I couldn’t see for the glory of that light, being led by the hand of those who were with me, I came into Damascus.

translations.kjv: And one Ananias, a devout man according to the law, having a good report of all the Jews which dwelt there,
translations.ylt: and a certain one, Ananias, a pious man according to the law, being testified to by all the Jews dwelling there,
translations.web: “One Ananias, a devout man according to the law, well reported of by all the Jews who lived in Damascus,

translations.kjv: Came unto me, and stood, and said unto me, Brother Saul, receive thy sight. And the same hour I looked up upon him.
translations.ylt: having come unto me and stood by me, said to me, Saul, brother, look up; and I the same hour did look up to him;
translations.web: came to me, and standing by me said to me, ‘Brother Saul, receive your sight!’ In that very hour I looked up at him.

translations.kjv: And he said, The God of our fathers hath chosen thee, that thou shouldest know his will, and see that Just One, and shouldest hear the voice of his mouth.
translations.ylt: and he said, The God of our fathers did choose thee beforehand to know His will, and to see the Righteous One, and to hear a voice out of his mouth,
translations.web: He said, ‘The God of our fathers has appointed you to know his will, and to see the Righteous One, and to hear a voice from his mouth.

translations.kjv: For thou shalt be his witness unto all men of what thou hast seen and heard.
translations.ylt: because thou shalt be his witness unto all men of what thou hast seen and heard;
translations.web: For you will be a witness for him to all men of what you have seen and heard.

translations.kjv: And now why tarriest thou? arise, and be baptized, and wash away thy sins, calling on the name of the Lord.
translations.ylt: and now, why tarriest thou? having risen, baptize thyself, and wash away thy sins, calling upon the name of the Lord.
translations.web: Now why do you wait? Arise, be baptized, and wash away your sins, calling on the name of the Lord.’

translations.kjv: And it came to pass, that, when I was come again to Jerusalem, even while I prayed in the temple, I was in a trance;
translations.ylt: `And it came to pass when I returned to Jerusalem, and while I was praying in the temple, I came into a trance,
translations.web: “When I had returned to Jerusalem and while I prayed in the temple, I fell into a trance

translations.kjv: And saw him saying unto me, Make haste, and get thee quickly out of Jerusalem: for they will not receive thy testimony concerning me.
translations.ylt: and I saw him saying to me, Haste and go forth in haste out of Jerusalem, because they will not receive thy testimony concerning me;
translations.web: and saw him saying to me, ‘Hurry and get out of Jerusalem quickly, because they will not receive testimony concerning me from you.’

translations.kjv: And I said, Lord, they know that I imprisoned and beat in every synagogue them that believed on thee:
translations.ylt: and I said, Lord, they--they know that I was imprisoning and was scourging in every synagogue those believing on thee;
translations.web: I said, ‘Lord, they themselves know that I imprisoned and beat in every synagogue those who believed in you.

translations.kjv: And when the blood of thy martyr Stephen was shed, I also was standing by, and consenting unto his death, and kept the raiment of them that slew him.
translations.ylt: and when the blood of thy witness Stephen was being poured forth, I also was standing by and assenting to his death, and keeping the garments of those putting him to death;
translations.web: When the blood of Stephen, your witness, was shed, I also was standing by, consenting to his death, and guarding the cloaks of those who killed him.’

translations.kjv: And he said unto me, Depart: for I will send thee far hence unto the Gentiles.
translations.ylt: and he said unto me, Go, because to nations far off I will send thee.'
translations.web: “He said to me, ‘Depart, for I will send you out far from here to the Gentiles.’ ”

translations.kjv: And they gave him audience unto this word, and then lifted up their voices, and said, Away with such a fellow from the earth: for it is not fit that he should live.
translations.ylt: And they were hearing him unto this word, and they lifted up their voice, saying, `Away from the earth with such an one; for it is not fit for him to live.'
translations.web: They listened to him until he said that; then they lifted up their voice and said, “Rid the earth of this fellow, for he isn’t fit to live!”

translations.kjv: And as they cried out, and cast off their clothes, and threw dust into the air,
translations.ylt: And they crying out and casting up their garments, and throwing dust into the air,
translations.web: As they cried out, threw off their cloaks, and threw dust into the air,

translations.kjv: The chief captain commanded him to be brought into the castle, and bade that he should be examined by scourging; that he might know wherefore they cried so against him.
translations.ylt: the chief captain commanded him to be brought into the castle, saying, `By scourges let him be examined;' that he might know for what cause they were crying so against him.
translations.web: the commanding officer commanded him to be brought into the barracks, ordering him to be examined by scourging, that he might know for what crime they shouted against him like that.

translations.kjv: And as they bound him with thongs, Paul said unto the centurion that stood by, Is it lawful for you to scourge a man that is a Roman, and uncondemned?
translations.ylt: And as he was stretching him with the thongs, Paul said unto the centurion who was standing by, `A man, a Roman, uncondemned--is it lawful to you to scourge;'
translations.web: When they had tied him up with straps, Paul asked the centurion who stood by, “Is it lawful for you to scourge a man who is a Roman, and not found guilty?”

translations.kjv: When the centurion heard that, he went and told the chief captain, saying, Take heed what thou doest: for this man is a Roman.
translations.ylt: and the centurion having heard, having gone near to the chief captain, told, saying, `Take heed what thou art about to do, for this man is a Roman;'
translations.web: When the centurion heard it, he went to the commanding officer and told him, “Watch what you are about to do, for this man is a Roman!”

translations.kjv: Then the chief captain came, and said unto him, Tell me, art thou a Roman? He said, Yea.
translations.ylt: and the chief captain having come near, said to him, `Tell me, art thou a Roman?' and he said, `Yes;'
translations.web: The commanding officer came and asked him, “Tell me, are you a Roman?” He said, “Yes.”

translations.kjv: And the chief captain answered, With a great sum obtained I this freedom. And Paul said, But I was free born.
translations.ylt: and the chief captain answered, `I, with a great sum, did obtain this citizenship;' but Paul said, `But I have been even born so.'
translations.web: The commanding officer answered, “I bought my citizenship for a great price.” Paul said, “But I was born a Roman.”

translations.kjv: Then straightway they departed from him which should have examined him: and the chief captain also was afraid, after he knew that he was a Roman, and because he had bound him.
translations.ylt: Immediately, therefore, they departed from him who are about to examine him, and the chief captain also was afraid, having learned that he is a Roman, and because he had bound him,
translations.web: Immediately those who were about to examine him departed from him, and the commanding officer also was afraid when he realized that he was a Roman, because he had bound him.

translations.kjv: On the morrow, because he would have known the certainty wherefore he was accused of the Jews, he loosed him from his bands, and commanded the chief priests and all their council to appear, and brought Paul down, and set him before them.
translations.ylt: and on the morrow, intending to know the certainty wherefore he is accused by the Jews, he did loose him from the bonds, and commanded the chief priests and all their sanhedrim to come, and having brought down Paul, he set him before them.
translations.web: But on the next day, desiring to know the truth about why he was accused by the Jews, he freed him from the bonds and commanded the chief priests and all the council to come together, and brought Paul down and set him before them.

translations.kjv: And Paul, earnestly beholding the council, said, Men and brethren, I have lived in all good conscience before God until this day.
translations.ylt: And Paul having earnestly beheld the sanhedrim, said, `Men, brethren, I in all good conscience have lived to God unto this day;'
translations.web: Paul, looking steadfastly at the council, said, “Brothers, I have lived before God in all good conscience until today.”

translations.kjv: And the high priest Ananias commanded them that stood by him to smite him on the mouth.
translations.ylt: and the chief priest Ananias commanded those standing by him to smite him on the mouth,
translations.web: The high priest, Ananias, commanded those who stood by him to strike him on the mouth.

translations.kjv: Then said Paul unto him, God shall smite thee, thou whited wall: for sittest thou to judge me after the law, and commandest me to be smitten contrary to the law?
translations.ylt: then Paul said unto him, `God is about to smite thee, thou whitewashed wall, and thou--thou dost sit judging me according to the law, and, violating law, dost order me to be smitten!'
translations.web: Then Paul said to him, “God will strike you, you whitewashed wall! Do you sit to judge me according to the law, and command me to be struck contrary to the law?”

translations.kjv: And they that stood by said, Revilest thou God’s high priest?
translations.ylt: And those who stood by said, `The chief priest of God dost thou revile?'
translations.web: Those who stood by said, “Do you malign God’s high priest?”

translations.kjv: Then said Paul, I wist not, brethren, that he was the high priest: for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people.
translations.ylt: and Paul said, `I did not know, brethren, that he is chief priest: for it hath been written, Of the ruler of thy people thou shalt not speak evil;'
translations.web: Paul said, “I didn’t know, brothers, that he was high priest. For it is written, ‘You shall not speak evil of a ruler of your people.’”

translations.kjv: But when Paul perceived that the one part were Sadducees, and the other Pharisees, he cried out in the council, Men and brethren, I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee: of the hope and resurrection of the dead I am called in question.
translations.ylt: and Paul having known that the one part are Sadducees, and the other Pharisees, cried out in the sanhedrim, `Men, brethren, I am a Pharisee--son of a Pharisee--concerning hope and rising again of dead men I am judged.'
translations.web: But when Paul perceived that the one part were Sadducees and the other Pharisees, he cried out in the council, “Men and brothers, I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees. Concerning the hope and resurrection of the dead I am being judged!”

translations.kjv: And when he had so said, there arose a dissension between the Pharisees and the Sadducees: and the multitude was divided.
translations.ylt: And he having spoken this, there came a dissension of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees, and the crowd was divided,
translations.web: When he had said this, an argument arose between the Pharisees and Sadducees, and the crowd was divided.

translations.kjv: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, neither angel, nor spirit: but the Pharisees confess both.
translations.ylt: for Sadducees, indeed, say there is no rising again, nor messenger, nor spirit, but Pharisees confess both.
translations.web: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, nor angel, nor spirit; but the Pharisees confess all of these.

translations.kjv: And there arose a great cry: and the scribes that were of the Pharisees’ part arose, and strove, saying, We find no evil in this man: but if a spirit or an angel hath spoken to him, let us not fight against God.
translations.ylt: And there came a great cry, and the scribes of the Pharisees' part having arisen, were striving, saying, `No evil do we find in this man; and if a spirit spake to him, or a messenger, we may not fight against God;'
translations.web: A great clamor arose, and some of the scribes of the Pharisees’ part stood up, and contended, saying, “We find no evil in this man. But if a spirit or angel has spoken to him, let’s not fight against God!”

translations.kjv: And when there arose a great dissension, the chief captain, fearing lest Paul should have been pulled in pieces of them, commanded the soldiers to go down, and to take him by force from among them, and to bring him into the castle.
translations.ylt: and a great dissension having come, the chief captain having been afraid lest Paul may be pulled to pieces by them, commanded the soldiery, having gone down, to take him by force out of the midst of them, and to bring him to the castle.
translations.web: When a great argument arose, the commanding officer, fearing that Paul would be torn in pieces by them, commanded the soldiers to go down and take him by force from among them and bring him into the barracks.

translations.kjv: And the night following the Lord stood by him, and said, Be of good cheer, Paul: for as thou hast testified of me in Jerusalem, so must thou bear witness also at Rome.
translations.ylt: And on the following night, the Lord having stood by him, said, `Take courage, Paul, for as thou didst fully testify the things concerning me at Jerusalem, so it behoveth thee also at Rome to testify.'
translations.web: The following night, the Lord stood by him and said, “Cheer up, Paul, for as you have testified about me at Jerusalem, so you must testify also at Rome.”

translations.kjv: And when it was day, certain of the Jews banded together, and bound themselves under a curse, saying that they would neither eat nor drink till they had killed Paul.
translations.ylt: And day having come, certain of the Jews having made a concourse, did anathematize themselves, saying neither to eat nor to drink till they may kill Paul;
translations.web: When it was day, some of the Jews banded together and bound themselves under a curse, saying that they would neither eat nor drink until they had killed Paul.

translations.kjv: And they were more than forty which had made this conspiracy.
translations.ylt: and they were more than forty who made this conspiracy by oath,
translations.web: There were more than forty people who had made this conspiracy.

translations.kjv: And they came to the chief priests and elders, and said, We have bound ourselves under a great curse, that we will eat nothing until we have slain Paul.
translations.ylt: who having come near to the chief priests and to the elders said, `With an anathema we did anathematize ourselves--to taste nothing till we have killed Paul;
translations.web: They came to the chief priests and the elders, and said, “We have bound ourselves under a great curse to taste nothing until we have killed Paul.

translations.kjv: Now therefore ye with the council signify to the chief captain that he bring him down unto you to morrow, as though ye would enquire something more perfectly concerning him: and we, or ever he come near, are ready to kill him.
translations.ylt: now, therefore, ye, signify ye to the chief captain, with the sanhedrim, that to-morrow he may bring him down unto you, as being about to know more exactly the things concerning him; and we, before his coming nigh, are ready to put him to death.'
translations.web: Now therefore, you with the council inform the commanding officer that he should bring him down to you tomorrow, as though you were going to judge his case more exactly. We are ready to kill him before he comes near.”

translations.kjv: And when Paul’s sister’s son heard of their lying in wait, he went and entered into the castle, and told Paul.
translations.ylt: And the son of Paul's sister having heard of the lying in wait, having gone and entered into the castle, told Paul,
translations.web: But Paul’s sister’s son heard they were lying in wait, and he came and entered into the barracks and told Paul.

translations.kjv: Then Paul called one of the centurions unto him, and said, Bring this young man unto the chief captain: for he hath a certain thing to tell him.
translations.ylt: and Paul having called near one of the centurions, said, `This young man lead unto the chief captain, for he hath something to tell him.'
translations.web: Paul summoned one of the centurions and said, “Bring this young man to the commanding officer, for he has something to tell him.”

translations.kjv: So he took him, and brought him to the chief captain, and said, Paul the prisoner called me unto him, and prayed me to bring this young man unto thee, who hath something to say unto thee.
translations.ylt: He indeed, then, having taken him, brought him unto the chief captain, and saith, `The prisoner Paul, having called me near, asked me this young man to bring unto thee, having something to say to thee.'
translations.web: So he took him and brought him to the commanding officer and said, “Paul, the prisoner, summoned me and asked me to bring this young man to you. He has something to tell you.”

translations.kjv: Then the chief captain took him by the hand, and went with him aside privately, and asked him, What is that thou hast to tell me?
translations.ylt: And the chief captain having taken him by the hand, and having withdrawn by themselves, inquired, `What is that which thou hast to tell me?'
translations.web: The commanding officer took him by the hand, and going aside, asked him privately, “What is it that you have to tell me?”

translations.kjv: And he said, The Jews have agreed to desire thee that thou wouldest bring down Paul to morrow into the council, as though they would enquire somewhat of him more perfectly.
translations.ylt: and he said--`The Jews agreed to request thee, that to-morrow to the sanhedrim thou mayest bring down Paul, as being about to enquire something more exactly concerning him;
translations.web: He said, “The Jews have agreed to ask you to bring Paul down to the council tomorrow, as though intending to inquire somewhat more accurately concerning him.

translations.kjv: But do not thou yield unto them: for there lie in wait for him of them more than forty men, which have bound themselves with an oath, that they will neither eat nor drink till they have killed him: and now are they ready, looking for a promise from thee.
translations.ylt: thou, therefore, mayest thou not yield to them, for there lie in wait for him of them more than forty men, who did anathematize themselves--not to eat nor to drink till they kill him, and now they are ready, waiting for the promise from thee.'
translations.web: Therefore don’t yield to them, for more than forty men lie in wait for him, who have bound themselves under a curse to neither eat nor drink until they have killed him. Now they are ready, looking for the promise from you.”

translations.kjv: So the chief captain then let the young man depart, and charged him, See thou tell no man that thou hast shewed these things to me.
translations.ylt: The chief captain, then, indeed, let the young man go, having charged him to tell no one, `that these things thou didst shew unto me;'
translations.web: So the commanding officer let the young man go, charging him, “Tell no one that you have revealed these things to me.”

translations.kjv: And he called unto him two centurions, saying, Make ready two hundred soldiers to go to Cesarea, and horsemen threescore and ten, and spearmen two hundred, at the third hour of the night;
translations.ylt: and having called near a certain two of the centurions, he said, `Make ready soldiers two hundred, that they may go on unto Caesarea, and horsemen seventy, and spearmen two hundred, from the third hour of the night;
translations.web: He called to himself two of the centurions, and said, “Prepare two hundred soldiers to go as far as Caesarea, with seventy horsemen and two hundred men armed with spears, at the third hour of the night.”

translations.kjv: And provide them beasts, that they may set Paul on, and bring him safe unto Felix the governor.
translations.ylt: beasts also provide, that, having set Paul on, they may bring him safe unto Felix the governor;'
translations.web: He asked them to provide mounts, that they might set Paul on one, and bring him safely to Felix the governor.

translations.kjv: And he wrote a letter after this manner:
translations.ylt: he having written a letter after this description:
translations.web: He wrote a letter like this:

translations.kjv: Claudius Lysias unto the most excellent governor Felix sendeth greeting.
translations.ylt: `Claudius Lysias, to the most noble governor Felix, hail:
translations.web: “Claudius Lysias to the most excellent governor Felix: Greetings.

translations.kjv: This man was taken of the Jews, and should have been killed of them: then came I with an army, and rescued him, having understood that he was a Roman.
translations.ylt: This man having been taken by the Jews, and being about to be killed by them--having come with the soldiery, I rescued him, having learned that he is a Roman;
translations.web: “This man was seized by the Jews, and was about to be killed by them when I came with the soldiers and rescued him, having learned that he was a Roman.

translations.kjv: And when I would have known the cause wherefore they accused him, I brought him forth into their council:
translations.ylt: and, intending to know the cause for which they were accusing him, I brought him down to their sanhedrim,
translations.web: Desiring to know the cause why they accused him, I brought him down to their council.

translations.kjv: Whom I perceived to be accused of questions of their law, but to have nothing laid to his charge worthy of death or of bonds.
translations.ylt: whom I found accused concerning questions of their law, and having no accusation worthy of death or bonds;
translations.web: I found him to be accused about questions of their law, but not to be charged with anything worthy of death or of imprisonment.

translations.kjv: And when it was told me how that the Jews laid wait for the man, I sent straightway to thee, and gave commandment to his accusers also to say before thee what they had against him. Farewell.
translations.ylt: and a plot having been intimated to me against this man--about to be of the Jews--at once I sent unto thee, having given command also to the accusers to say the things against him before thee; be strong.'
translations.web: When I was told that the Jews lay in wait for the man, I sent him to you immediately, charging his accusers also to bring their accusations against him before you. Farewell.”

translations.kjv: Then the soldiers, as it was commanded them, took Paul, and brought him by night to Antipatris.
translations.ylt: Then, indeed, the soldiers according to that directed them, having taken up Paul, brought him through the night to Antipatris,
translations.web: So the soldiers, carrying out their orders, took Paul and brought him by night to Antipatris.

translations.kjv: On the morrow they left the horsemen to go with him, and returned to the castle:
translations.ylt: and on the morrow, having suffered the horsemen to go on with him, they returned to the castle;
translations.web: But on the next day they left the horsemen to go with him, and returned to the barracks.

translations.kjv: Who, when they came to Cesarea, and delivered the epistle to the governor, presented Paul also before him.
translations.ylt: those having entered into Caesarea, and delivered the letter to the governor, did present also Paul to him.
translations.web: When they came to Caesarea and delivered the letter to the governor, they also presented Paul to him.

translations.kjv: And when the governor had read the letter, he asked of what province he was. And when he understood that he was of Cilicia;
translations.ylt: And the governor having read it, and inquired of what province he is, and understood that he is from Cilicia;
translations.web: When the governor had read it, he asked what province he was from. When he understood that he was from Cilicia, he said,

translations.kjv: I will hear thee, said he, when thine accusers are also come. And he commanded him to be kept in Herod’s judgment hall.
translations.ylt: `I will hear thee--said he--when thine accusers also may have come;' he also commanded him to be kept in the praetorium of Herod.
translations.web: “I will hear you fully when your accusers also arrive.” He commanded that he be kept in Herod’s palace.

translations.kjv: And after five days Ananias the high priest descended with the elders, and with a certain orator named Tertullus, who informed the governor against Paul.
translations.ylt: And after five days came down the chief priest Ananias, with the elders, and a certain orator--Tertullus, and they made manifest to the governor the things against Paul;
translations.web: After five days, the high priest, Ananias, came down with certain elders and an orator, one Tertullus. They informed the governor against Paul.

translations.kjv: And when he was called forth, Tertullus began to accuse him, saying, Seeing that by thee we enjoy great quietness, and that very worthy deeds are done unto this nation by thy providence,
translations.ylt: and he having been called, Tertullus began to accuse him, saying, `Much peace enjoying through thee, and worthy deeds being done to this nation through thy forethought,
translations.web: When he was called, Tertullus began to accuse him, saying, “Seeing that by you we enjoy much peace, and that prosperity is coming to this nation by your foresight,

translations.kjv: We accept it always, and in all places, most noble Felix, with all thankfulness.
translations.ylt: always, also, and everywhere we receive it, most noble Felix, with all thankfulness;
translations.web: we accept it in all ways and in all places, most excellent Felix, with all thankfulness.

translations.kjv: Notwithstanding, that I be not further tedious unto thee, I pray thee that thou wouldest hear us of thy clemency a few words.
translations.ylt: and that I may not be further tedious to thee, I pray thee to hear us concisely in thy gentleness;
translations.web: But that I don’t delay you, I entreat you to bear with us and hear a few words.

translations.kjv: For we have found this man a pestilent fellow, and a mover of sedition among all the Jews throughout the world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes:
translations.ylt: for having found this man a pestilence, and moving a dissension to all the Jews through the world--a ringleader also of the sect of the Nazarenes--
translations.web: For we have found this man to be a plague, an instigator of insurrections among all the Jews throughout the world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes.

translations.kjv: Who also hath gone about to profane the temple: whom we took, and would have judged according to our law.
translations.ylt: who also the temple did try to profane, whom also we took, and according to our law did wish to judge,
translations.web: He even tried to profane the temple, and we arrested him.

translations.kjv: Commanding his accusers to come unto thee: by examining of whom thyself mayest take knowledge of all these things, whereof we accuse him.
translations.ylt: having commanded his accusers to come to thee, from whom thou mayest be able, thyself having examined, to know concerning all these things of which we accuse him;'
translations.web: By examining him yourself you may ascertain all these things of which we accuse him.”

translations.kjv: And the Jews also assented, saying that these things were so.
translations.ylt: and the Jews also agreed, professing these things to be so.
translations.web: The Jews also joined in the attack, affirming that these things were so.

translations.kjv: Then Paul, after that the governor had beckoned unto him to speak, answered, Forasmuch as I know that thou hast been of many years a judge unto this nation, I do the more cheerfully answer for myself:
translations.ylt: And Paul answered--the governor having beckoned to him to speak--`Knowing that for many years thou hast been a judge to this nation, the more cheerfully the things concerning myself I do answer;
translations.web: When the governor had beckoned to him to speak, Paul answered, “Because I know that you have been a judge of this nation for many years, I cheerfully make my defense,

translations.kjv: Because that thou mayest understand, that there are yet but twelve days since I went up to Jerusalem for to worship.
translations.ylt: thou being able to know that it is not more than twelve days to me since I went up to worship in Jerusalem,
translations.web: seeing that you can verify that it is not more than twelve days since I went up to worship at Jerusalem.

translations.kjv: And they neither found me in the temple disputing with any man, neither raising up the people, neither in the synagogues, nor in the city:
translations.ylt: and neither in the temple did they find me reasoning with any one, or making a dissension of the multitude, nor in the synagogues, nor in the city;
translations.web: In the temple they didn’t find me disputing with anyone or stirring up a crowd, either in the synagogues or in the city.

translations.kjv: Neither can they prove the things whereof they now accuse me.
translations.ylt: nor are they able to prove against me the things concerning which they now accuse me.
translations.web: Nor can they prove to you the things of which they now accuse me.

translations.kjv: But this I confess unto thee, that after the way which they call heresy, so worship I the God of my fathers, believing all things which are written in the law and in the prophets:
translations.ylt: `And I confess this to thee, that, according to the way that they call a sect, so serve I the God of the fathers, believing all things that in the law and the prophets have been written,
translations.web: But this I confess to you, that according to the Way, which they call a sect, so I serve the God of our fathers, believing all things which are according to the law, and which are written in the prophets;

translations.kjv: And have hope toward God, which they themselves also allow, that there shall be a resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust.
translations.ylt: having hope toward God, which they themselves also wait for, that there is about to be a rising again of the dead, both of righteous and unrighteous;
translations.web: having hope toward God, which these also themselves look for, that there will be a resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust.

translations.kjv: And herein do I exercise myself, to have always a conscience void of offence toward God, and toward men.
translations.ylt: and in this I do exercise myself, to have a conscience void of offence toward God and men always.
translations.web: In this I also practice always having a conscience void of offense toward God and men.

translations.kjv: Now after many years I came to bring alms to my nation, and offerings.
translations.ylt: `And after many years I came, about to do kind acts to my nation, and offerings,
translations.web: Now after some years, I came to bring gifts for the needy to my nation, and offerings;

translations.kjv: Whereupon certain Jews from Asia found me purified in the temple, neither with multitude, nor with tumult.
translations.ylt: in which certain Jews from Asia did find me purified in the temple, not with multitude, nor with tumult,
translations.web: amid which certain Jews from Asia found me purified in the temple, not with a mob, nor with turmoil.

translations.kjv: Who ought to have been here before thee, and object, if they had ought against me.
translations.ylt: whom it behoveth to be present before thee, and to accuse, if they had anything against me,
translations.web: They ought to have been here before you and to make accusation if they had anything against me.

translations.kjv: Or else let these same here say, if they have found any evil doing in me, while I stood before the council,
translations.ylt: or let these same say if they found any unrighteousness in me in my standing before the sanhedrim,
translations.web: Or else let these men themselves say what injustice they found in me when I stood before the council,

translations.kjv: Except it be for this one voice, that I cried standing among them, Touching the resurrection of the dead I am called in question by you this day.
translations.ylt: except concerning this one voice, in which I cried, standing among them--Concerning a rising again of the dead I am judged to-day by you.'
translations.web: unless it is for this one thing that I cried standing among them, ‘Concerning the resurrection of the dead I am being judged before you today!’”

translations.kjv: And when Felix heard these things, having more perfect knowledge of that way, he deferred them, and said, When Lysias the chief captain shall come down, I will know the uttermost of your matter.
translations.ylt: And having heard these things, Felix delayed them--having known more exactly of the things concerning the way--saying, `When Lysias the chief captain may come down, I will know fully the things concerning you;'
translations.web: But Felix, having more exact knowledge concerning the Way, deferred them, saying, “When Lysias, the commanding officer, comes down, I will decide your case.”

translations.kjv: And he commanded a centurion to keep Paul, and to let him have liberty, and that he should forbid none of his acquaintance to minister or come unto him.
translations.ylt: having given also a direction to the centurion to keep Paul, to let him also have liberty, and to forbid none of his own friends to minister or to come near to him.
translations.web: He ordered the centurion that Paul should be kept in custody and should have some privileges, and not to forbid any of his friends to serve him or to visit him.

translations.kjv: And after certain days, when Felix came with his wife Drusilla, which was a Jewess, he sent for Paul, and heard him concerning the faith in Christ.
translations.ylt: And after certain days, Felix having come with Drusilla his wife, being a Jewess, he sent for Paul, and heard him concerning the faith toward Christ,
translations.web: After some days, Felix came with Drusilla his wife, who was a Jewess, and sent for Paul and heard him concerning the faith in Christ Jesus.

translations.kjv: And as he reasoned of righteousness, temperance, and judgment to come, Felix trembled, and answered, Go thy way for this time; when I have a convenient season, I will call for thee.
translations.ylt: and he reasoning concerning righteousness, and temperance, and the judgment that is about to be, Felix, having become afraid, answered, `For the present be going, and having got time, I will call for thee;'
translations.web: As he reasoned about righteousness, self-control, and the judgment to come, Felix was terrified, and answered, “Go your way for this time, and when it is convenient for me, I will summon you.”

translations.kjv: He hoped also that money should have been given him of Paul, that he might loose him: wherefore he sent for him the oftener, and communed with him.
translations.ylt: and at the same time also hoping that money shall be given to him by Paul, that he may release him, therefore, also sending for him the oftener, he was conversing with him;
translations.web: Meanwhile, he also hoped that money would be given to him by Paul, that he might release him. Therefore also he sent for him more often and talked with him.

translations.kjv: But after two years Porcius Festus came into Felix’ room: and Felix, willing to shew the Jews a pleasure, left Paul bound.
translations.ylt: and two years having been fulfilled, Felix received a successor, Porcius Festus; Felix also willing to lay a favour on the Jews, left Paul bound.
translations.web: But when two years were fulfilled, Felix was succeeded by Porcius Festus, and desiring to gain favor with the Jews, Felix left Paul in bonds.

translations.kjv: Now when Festus was come into the province, after three days he ascended from Cesarea to Jerusalem.
translations.ylt: Festus, therefore, having come into the province, after three days went up to Jerusalem from Caesarea,
translations.web: Festus therefore, having come into the province, after three days went up to Jerusalem from Caesarea.

translations.kjv: Then the high priest and the chief of the Jews informed him against Paul, and besought him,
translations.ylt: and the chief priest and the principal men of the Jews made manifest to him the things against Paul, and were calling on him,
translations.web: Then the high priest and the principal men of the Jews informed him against Paul, and they begged him,

translations.kjv: And desired favour against him, that he would send for him to Jerusalem, laying wait in the way to kill him.
translations.ylt: asking favour against him, that he may send for him to Jerusalem, making an ambush to put him to death in the way.
translations.web: asking a favor against him, that he would summon him to Jerusalem, plotting to kill him on the way.

translations.kjv: But Festus answered, that Paul should be kept at Cesarea, and that he himself would depart shortly thither.
translations.ylt: Then, indeed, Festus answered that Paul is kept in Caesarea, and himself is about speedily to go on thither,
translations.web: However Festus answered that Paul should be kept in custody at Caesarea, and that he himself was about to depart shortly.

translations.kjv: Let them therefore, said he, which among you are able, go down with me, and accuse this man, if there be any wickedness in him.
translations.ylt: `Therefore those able among you--saith he--having come down together, if there be anything in this man--let them accuse him;'
translations.web: “Let them therefore”, he said, “that are in power among you go down with me, and if there is anything wrong in the man, let them accuse him.”

translations.kjv: And when he had tarried among them more than ten days, he went down unto Cesarea; and the next day sitting on the judgment seat commanded Paul to be brought.
translations.ylt: and having tarried among them more than ten days, having gone down to Caesarea, on the morrow having sat upon the tribunal, he commanded Paul to be brought;
translations.web: When he had stayed among them more than ten days, he went down to Caesarea, and on the next day he sat on the judgment seat, and commanded Paul to be brought.

translations.kjv: And when he was come, the Jews which came down from Jerusalem stood round about, and laid many and grievous complaints against Paul, which they could not prove.
translations.ylt: and he having come, there stood round about the Jews who have come down from Jerusalem--many and weighty charges they are bringing against Paul, which they were not able to prove,
translations.web: When he had come, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood around him, bringing against him many and grievous charges which they could not prove,

translations.kjv: While he answered for himself, Neither against the law of the Jews, neither against the temple, nor yet against Cesar, have I offended any thing at all.
translations.ylt: he making defence--`Neither in regard to the law of the Jews, nor in regard to the temple, nor in regard to Caesar--did I commit any sin.'
translations.web: while he said in his defense, “Neither against the law of the Jews, nor against the temple, nor against Caesar, have I sinned at all.”

translations.kjv: But Festus, willing to do the Jews a pleasure, answered Paul, and said, Wilt thou go up to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these things before me?
translations.ylt: And Festus willing to lay on the Jews a favour, answering Paul, said, `Art thou willing, to Jerusalem having gone up, there concerning these things to be judged before me?'
translations.web: But Festus, desiring to gain favor with the Jews, answered Paul and said, “Are you willing to go up to Jerusalem and be judged by me there concerning these things?”

translations.kjv: Then said Paul, I stand at Cesar’s judgment seat, where I ought to be judged: to the Jews have I done no wrong, as thou very well knowest.
translations.ylt: and Paul said, `At the tribunal of Caesar I am standing, where it behoveth me to be judged; to Jews I did no unrighteousness, as thou dost also very well know;
translations.web: But Paul said, “I am standing before Caesar’s judgment seat, where I ought to be tried. I have done no wrong to the Jews, as you also know very well.

translations.kjv: For if I be an offender, or have committed any thing worthy of death, I refuse not to die: but if there be none of these things whereof these accuse me, no man may deliver me unto them. I appeal unto Cesar.
translations.ylt: for if indeed I am unrighteous, and anything worthy of death have done, I deprecate not to die; and if there is none of the things of which these accuse me, no one is able to make a favour of me to them; to Caesar I appeal!'
translations.web: For if I have done wrong and have committed anything worthy of death, I don’t refuse to die; but if none of those things is true that they accuse me of, no one can give me up to them. I appeal to Caesar!”

translations.kjv: Then Festus, when he had conferred with the council, answered, Hast thou appealed unto Cesar? unto Cesar shalt thou go.
translations.ylt: then Festus, having communed with the council, answered, `To Caesar thou hast appealed; to Caesar thou shalt go.'
translations.web: Then Festus, when he had conferred with the council, answered, “You have appealed to Caesar. To Caesar you shall go.”

translations.kjv: And after certain days king Agrippa and Bernice came unto Cesarea to salute Festus.
translations.ylt: And certain days having passed, Agrippa the king, and Bernice, came down to Caesarea saluting Festus,
translations.web: Now when some days had passed, King Agrippa and Bernice arrived at Caesarea and greeted Festus.

translations.kjv: And when they had been there many days, Festus declared Paul’s cause unto the king, saying, There is a certain man left in bonds by Felix:
translations.ylt: and as they were continuing there more days, Festus submitted to the king the things concerning Paul, saying, `There is a certain man, left by Felix, a prisoner,
translations.web: As he stayed there many days, Festus laid Paul’s case before the king, saying, “There is a certain man left a prisoner by Felix;

translations.kjv: About whom, when I was at Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews informed me, desiring to have judgment against him.
translations.ylt: about whom, in my being at Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews laid information, asking a decision against him,
translations.web: about whom, when I was at Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews informed me, asking for a sentence against him.

translations.kjv: To whom I answered, It is not the manner of the Romans to deliver any man to die, before that he which is accused have the accusers face to face, and have licence to answer for himself concerning the crime laid against him.
translations.ylt: unto whom I answered, that it is not a custom of Romans to make a favour of any man to die, before that he who is accused may have the accusers face to face, and may receive place of defence in regard to the charge laid against him.
translations.web: I answered them that it is not the custom of the Romans to give up any man to destruction before the accused has met the accusers face to face and has had opportunity to make his defense concerning the matter laid against him.

translations.kjv: Therefore, when they were come hither, without any delay on the morrow I sat on the judgment seat, and commanded the man to be brought forth.
translations.ylt: `They, therefore, having come together--I, making no delay, on the succeeding day having sat upon the tribunal, did command the man to be brought,
translations.web: When therefore they had come together here, I didn’t delay, but on the next day sat on the judgment seat and commanded the man to be brought.

translations.kjv: Against whom when the accusers stood up, they brought none accusation of such things as I supposed:
translations.ylt: concerning whom the accusers, having stood up, were bringing against him no accusation of the things I was thinking of,
translations.web: When the accusers stood up, they brought no charges against him of such things as I supposed;

translations.kjv: But had certain questions against him of their own superstition, and of one Jesus, which was dead, whom Paul affirmed to be alive.
translations.ylt: but certain questions concerning their own religion they had against him, and concerning a certain Jesus who was dead, whom Paul affirmed to be alive;
translations.web: but had certain questions against him about their own religion and about one Jesus, who was dead, whom Paul affirmed to be alive.

translations.kjv: And because I doubted of such manner of questions, I asked him whether he would go to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these matters.
translations.ylt: and I, doubting in regard to the question concerning this, said, If he would wish to go on to Jerusalem, and there to be judged concerning these things--
translations.web: Being perplexed how to inquire concerning these things, I asked whether he was willing to go to Jerusalem and there be judged concerning these matters.

translations.kjv: But when Paul had appealed to be reserved unto the hearing of Augustus, I commanded him to be kept till I might send him to Cesar.
translations.ylt: but Paul having appealed to be kept to the hearing of Sebastus, I did command him to be kept till I might send him unto Caesar.'
translations.web: But when Paul had appealed to be kept for the decision of the emperor, I commanded him to be kept until I could send him to Caesar.”

translations.kjv: Then Agrippa said unto Festus, I would also hear the man myself. To morrow, said he, thou shalt hear him.
translations.ylt: And Agrippa said unto Festus, `I was wishing also myself to hear the man;' and he said, `To-morrow thou shalt hear him;'
translations.web: Agrippa said to Festus, “I also would like to hear the man myself.” “Tomorrow,” he said, “you shall hear him.”

translations.kjv: And on the morrow, when Agrippa was come, and Bernice, with great pomp, and was entered into the place of hearing, with the chief captains, and principal men of the city, at Festus’ commandment Paul was brought forth.
translations.ylt: on the morrow, therefore--on the coming of Agrippa and Bernice with much display, and they having entered into the audience chamber, with the chief captains also, and the principal men of the city, and Festus having ordered--Paul was brought forth.
translations.web: So on the next day, when Agrippa and Bernice had come with great pomp, and they had entered into the place of hearing with the commanding officers and the principal men of the city, at the command of Festus, Paul was brought in.

translations.kjv: And Festus said, King Agrippa, and all men which are here present with us, ye see this man, about whom all the multitude of the Jews have dealt with me, both at Jerusalem, and also here, crying that he ought not to live any longer.
translations.ylt: And Festus said, `King Agrippa, and all men who are present with us, ye see this one, about whom all the multitude of the Jews did deal with me, both in Jerusalem and here, crying out, He ought not to live any longer;
translations.web: Festus said, “King Agrippa, and all men who are here present with us, you see this man about whom all the multitude of the Jews petitioned me, both at Jerusalem and here, crying that he ought not to live any longer.

translations.kjv: But when I found that he had committed nothing worthy of death, and that he himself hath appealed to Augustus, I have determined to send him.
translations.ylt: and I, having found him to have done nothing worthy of death, and he also himself having appealed to Sebastus, I decided to send him,
translations.web: But when I found that he had committed nothing worthy of death, and as he himself appealed to the emperor, I determined to send him,

translations.kjv: Of whom I have no certain thing to write unto my lord. Wherefore I have brought him forth before you, and specially before thee, O king Agrippa, that, after examination had, I might have somewhat to write.
translations.ylt: concerning whom I have no certain thing to write to my lord, wherefore I brought him forth before you, and specially before thee, king Agrippa, that the examination having been made, I may have something to write;
translations.web: of whom I have no certain thing to write to my lord. Therefore I have brought him out before you, and especially before you, King Agrippa, that, after examination I may have something to write.

translations.kjv: For it seemeth to me unreasonable to send a prisoner, and not withal to signify the crimes laid against him.
translations.ylt: for it doth seem to me irrational, sending a prisoner, not also to signify the charges against him.'
translations.web: For it seems to me unreasonable, in sending a prisoner, not to also specify the charges against him.”

translations.kjv: Then Agrippa said unto Paul, Thou art permitted to speak for thyself. Then Paul stretched forth the hand, and answered for himself:
translations.ylt: And Agrippa said unto Paul, `It is permitted to thee to speak for thyself;' then Paul having stretched forth the hand, was making a defence:
translations.web: Agrippa said to Paul, “You may speak for yourself.” Then Paul stretched out his hand, and made his defense.

translations.kjv: I think myself happy, king Agrippa, because I shall answer for myself this day before thee touching all the things whereof I am accused of the Jews:
translations.ylt: `Concerning all things of which I am accused by Jews, king Agrippa, I have thought myself happy, being about to make a defence before thee to-day,
translations.web: “I think myself happy, King Agrippa, that I am to make my defense before you today concerning all the things the Jews accuse me of,

translations.kjv: Especially because I know thee to be expert in all customs and questions which are among the Jews: wherefore I beseech thee to hear me patiently.
translations.ylt: especially knowing thee to be acquainted with all things--both customs and questions--among Jews; wherefore, I beseech thee, patiently to hear me.
translations.web: especially because you are expert in all customs and questions which are among the Jews. Therefore I beg you to hear me patiently.

translations.kjv: My manner of life from my youth, which was at the first among mine own nation at Jerusalem, know all the Jews;
translations.ylt: `The manner of my life then, indeed, from youth--which from the beginning was among my nation, in Jerusalem--know do all the Jews,
translations.web: “Indeed, all the Jews know my way of life from my youth up, which was from the beginning among my own nation and at Jerusalem;

translations.kjv: Which knew me from the beginning, if they would testify, that after the most straitest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.
translations.ylt: knowing me before from the first, (if they may be willing to testify,) that after the most exact sect of our worship, I lived a Pharisee;
translations.web: having known me from the first, if they are willing to testify, that after the strictest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.

translations.kjv: And now I stand and am judged for the hope of the promise made of God unto our fathers:
translations.ylt: and now for the hope of the promise made to the fathers by God, I have stood judged,
translations.web: Now I stand here to be judged for the hope of the promise made by God to our fathers,

translations.kjv: Unto which promise our twelve tribes, instantly serving God day and night, hope to come. For which hope’s sake, king Agrippa, I am accused of the Jews.
translations.ylt: to which our twelve tribes, intently night and day serving, do hope to come, concerning which hope I am accused, king Agrippa, by the Jews;
translations.web: which our twelve tribes, earnestly serving night and day, hope to attain. Concerning this hope I am accused by the Jews, King Agrippa!

translations.kjv: Why should it be thought a thing incredible with you, that God should raise the dead?
translations.ylt: why is it judged incredible with you, if God doth raise the dead?
translations.web: Why is it judged incredible with you if God does raise the dead?

translations.kjv: I verily thought with myself, that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.
translations.ylt: `I, indeed, therefore, thought with myself, that against the name of Jesus of Nazareth it behoved me many things to do,
translations.web: “I myself most certainly thought that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.

translations.kjv: Which thing I also did in Jerusalem: and many of the saints did I shut up in prison, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death, I gave my voice against them.
translations.ylt: which also I did in Jerusalem, and many of the saints I in prison did shut up, from the chief priests having received the authority; they also being put to death, I gave my vote against them,
translations.web: I also did this in Jerusalem. I both shut up many of the saints in prisons, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death I gave my vote against them.

translations.kjv: And I punished them oft in every synagogue, and compelled them to blaspheme; and being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto strange cities.
translations.ylt: and in every synagogue, often punishing them, I was constraining them to speak evil, being also exceedingly mad against them, I was also persecuting them even unto strange cities.
translations.web: Punishing them often in all the synagogues, I tried to make them blaspheme. Being exceedingly enraged against them, I persecuted them even to foreign cities.
