translations.kjv: Whereupon as I went to Damascus with authority and commission from the chief priests,
translations.ylt: `In which things, also, going on to Damascus--with authority and commission from the chief priests--
translations.web: “Whereupon as I traveled to Damascus with the authority and commission from the chief priests,

translations.kjv: At midday, O king, I saw in the way a light from heaven, above the brightness of the sun, shining round about me and them which journeyed with me.
translations.ylt: at mid-day, I saw in the way, O king, out of heaven, above the brightness of the sun, shining round about me a light--and those going on with me;
translations.web: at noon, O king, I saw on the way a light from the sky, brighter than the sun, shining around me and those who traveled with me.

translations.kjv: And when we were all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice speaking unto me, and saying in the Hebrew tongue, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me? it is hard for thee to kick against the pricks.
translations.ylt: and we all having fallen to the earth, I heard a voice speaking unto me, and saying in the Hebrew dialect, Saul, Saul, why me dost thou persecute? hard for thee against pricks to kick!
translations.web: When we had all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice saying to me in the Hebrew language, ‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me? It is hard for you to kick against the goads.’

translations.kjv: And I said, Who art thou, Lord? And he said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest.
translations.ylt: `And I said, Who art thou, Lord? and he said, I am Jesus whom thou dost persecute;
translations.web: “I said, ‘Who are you, Lord?’ “He said, ‘I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.

translations.kjv: But rise, and stand upon thy feet: for I have appeared unto thee for this purpose, to make thee a minister and a witness both of these things which thou hast seen, and of those things in the which I will appear unto thee;
translations.ylt: but rise, and stand upon thy feet, for for this I appeared to thee, to appoint thee an officer and a witness both of the things thou didst see, and of the things in which I will appear to thee,
translations.web: But arise, and stand on your feet, for I have appeared to you for this purpose: to appoint you a servant and a witness both of the things which you have seen and of the things which I will reveal to you;

translations.kjv: Delivering thee from the people, and from the Gentiles, unto whom now I send thee,
translations.ylt: delivering thee from the people, and the nations, to whom now I send thee,
translations.web: delivering you from the people and from the Gentiles, to whom I send you,

translations.kjv: To open their eyes, and to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan unto God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins, and inheritance among them which are sanctified by faith that is in me.
translations.ylt: to open their eyes, to turn them from darkness to light, and from the authority of the Adversary unto God, for their receiving forgiveness of sins, and a lot among those having been sanctified, by faith that is toward me.
translations.web: to open their eyes, that they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God, that they may receive remission of sins and an inheritance among those who are sanctified by faith in me.’

translations.kjv: Whereupon, O king Agrippa, I was not disobedient unto the heavenly vision:
translations.ylt: `Whereupon, king Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision,
translations.web: “Therefore, King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision,

translations.kjv: But shewed first unto them of Damascus, and at Jerusalem, and throughout all the coasts of Judea, and then to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, and do works meet for repentance.
translations.ylt: but to those in Damascus first, and to those in Jerusalem, to all the region also of Judea, and to the nations, I was preaching to reform, and to turn back unto God, doing works worthy of reformation;
translations.web: but declared first to them of Damascus, at Jerusalem, and throughout all the country of Judea, and also to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, doing works worthy of repentance.

translations.kjv: For these causes the Jews caught me in the temple, and went about to kill me.
translations.ylt: because of these things the Jews--having caught me in the temple--were endeavouring to kill me.
translations.web: For this reason the Jews seized me in the temple and tried to kill me.

translations.kjv: Having therefore obtained help of God, I continue unto this day, witnessing both to small and great, saying none other things than those which the prophets and Moses did say should come:
translations.ylt: `Having obtained, therefore, help from God, till this day, I have stood witnessing both to small and to great, saying nothing besides the things that both the prophets and Moses spake of as about to come,
translations.web: Having therefore obtained the help that is from God, I stand to this day testifying both to small and great, saying nothing but what the prophets and Moses said would happen,

translations.kjv: That Christ should suffer, and that he should be the first that should rise from the dead, and should shew light unto the people, and to the Gentiles.
translations.ylt: that the Christ is to suffer, whether first by a rising from the dead, he is about to proclaim light to the people and to the nations.'
translations.web: how the Christ must suffer, and how, by the resurrection of the dead, he would be first to proclaim light both to these people and to the Gentiles.”

translations.kjv: And as he thus spake for himself, Festus said with a loud voice, Paul, thou art beside thyself; much learning doth make thee mad.
translations.ylt: And, he thus making a defence, Festus with a loud voice said, `Thou art mad, Paul; much learning doth turn thee mad;'
translations.web: As he thus made his defense, Festus said with a loud voice, “Paul, you are crazy! Your great learning is driving you insane!”

translations.kjv: But he said, I am not mad, most noble Festus; but speak forth the words of truth and soberness.
translations.ylt: and he saith, `I am not mad, most noble Festus, but of truth and soberness the sayings I speak forth;
translations.web: But he said, “I am not crazy, most excellent Festus, but boldly declare words of truth and reasonableness.

translations.kjv: For the king knoweth of these things, before whom also I speak freely: for I am persuaded that none of these things are hidden from him; for this thing was not done in a corner.
translations.ylt: for the king doth know concerning these things, before whom also I speak boldly, for none of these things, I am persuaded, are hidden from him; for this thing hath not been done in a corner;
translations.web: For the king knows of these things, to whom also I speak freely. For I am persuaded that none of these things is hidden from him, for this has not been done in a corner.

translations.kjv: King Agrippa, believest thou the prophets? I know that thou believest.
translations.ylt: thou dost believe, king Agrippa, the prophets? I have known that thou dost believe!'
translations.web: King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know that you believe.”

translations.kjv: Then Agrippa said unto Paul, Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian.
translations.ylt: And Agrippa said unto Paul, `In a little thou dost persuade me to become a Christian!'
translations.web: Agrippa said to Paul, “With a little persuasion are you trying to make me a Christian?”

translations.kjv: And Paul said, I would to God, that not only thou, but also all that hear me this day, were both almost, and altogether such as I am, except these bonds.
translations.ylt: and Paul said, `I would have wished to God, both in a little, and in much, not only thee, but also all those hearing me to-day, to become such as I also am--except these bonds.'
translations.web: Paul said, “I pray to God, that whether with little or with much, not only you, but also all that hear me today, might become such as I am, except for these bonds.”

translations.kjv: And when he had thus spoken, the king rose up, and the governor, and Bernice, and they that sat with them:
translations.ylt: And, he having spoken these things, the king rose up, and the governor, Bernice also, and those sitting with them,
translations.web: The king rose up with the governor and Bernice, and those who sat with them.

translations.kjv: And when they were gone aside, they talked between themselves, saying, This man doeth nothing worthy of death or of bonds.
translations.ylt: and having withdrawn, they were speaking unto one another, saying--`This man doth nothing worthy of death or of bonds;'
translations.web: When they had withdrawn, they spoke to one another, saying, “This man does nothing worthy of death or of bonds.”

translations.kjv: Then said Agrippa unto Festus, This man might have been set at liberty, if he had not appealed unto Cesar.
translations.ylt: and Agrippa said to Festus, `This man might have been released if he had not appealed to Caesar.'
translations.web: Agrippa said to Festus, “This man might have been set free if he had not appealed to Caesar.”

translations.kjv: And when it was determined that we should sail into Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners unto one named Julius, a centurion of Augustus’ band.
translations.ylt: And when our sailing to Italy was determined, they were delivering up both Paul and certain others, prisoners, to a centurion, by name Julius, of the band of Sebastus,
translations.web: When it was determined that we should sail for Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners to a centurion named Julius, of the Augustan band.

translations.kjv: And entering into a ship of Adramyttium, we launched, meaning to sail by the coasts of Asia; one Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.
translations.ylt: and having embarked in a ship of Adramyttium, we, being about to sail by the coasts of Asia, did set sail, there being with us Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica,
translations.web: Embarking in a ship of Adramyttium, which was about to sail to places on the coast of Asia, we put to sea, Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica being with us.

translations.kjv: And the next day we touched at Sidon. And Julius courteously entreated Paul, and gave him liberty to go unto his friends to refresh himself.
translations.ylt: on the next day also we touched at Sidon, and Julius, courteously treating Paul, did permit him, having gone on unto friends, to receive their care.
translations.web: The next day, we touched at Sidon. Julius treated Paul kindly and gave him permission to go to his friends and refresh himself.

translations.kjv: And when we had launched from thence, we sailed under Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.
translations.ylt: And thence, having set sail, we sailed under Cyprus, because of the winds being contrary,
translations.web: Putting to sea from there, we sailed under the lee of Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.

translations.kjv: And when we had sailed over the sea of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, a city of Lycia.
translations.ylt: and having sailed over the sea over-against Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myria of Lycia,
translations.web: When we had sailed across the sea which is off Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, a city of Lycia.

translations.kjv: And there the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing into Italy; and he put us therein.
translations.ylt: and there the centurion having found a ship of Alexandria, sailing to Italy, did put us into it,
translations.web: There the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing for Italy, and he put us on board.

translations.kjv: And when we had sailed slowly many days, and scarce were come over against Cnidus, the wind not suffering us, we sailed under Crete, over against Salmone;
translations.ylt: and having sailed slowly many days, and with difficulty coming over-against Cnidus, the wind not suffering us, we sailed under Crete, over-against Salmone,
translations.web: When we had sailed slowly many days, and had come with difficulty opposite Cnidus, the wind not allowing us further, we sailed under the lee of Crete, opposite Salmone.

translations.kjv: And, hardly passing it, came unto a place which is called The fair havens; nigh whereunto was the city of Lasea.
translations.ylt: and hardly passing it, we came to a certain place called `Fair Havens,' nigh to which was the city of Lasaea.
translations.web: With difficulty sailing along it we came to a certain place called Fair Havens, near the city of Lasea.

translations.kjv: Now when much time was spent, and when sailing was now dangerous, because the fast was now already past, Paul admonished them,
translations.ylt: And much time being spent, and the sailing being now dangerous--because of the fast also being already past--Paul was admonishing,
translations.web: When much time had passed and the voyage was now dangerous because the Fast had now already gone by, Paul admonished them

translations.kjv: And said unto them, Sirs, I perceive that this voyage will be with hurt and much damage, not only of the lading and ship, but also of our lives.
translations.ylt: saying to them, `Men, I perceive that with hurt, and much damage, not only of the lading and of the ship, but also of our lives--the voyage is about to be;'
translations.web: and said to them, “Sirs, I perceive that the voyage will be with injury and much loss, not only of the cargo and the ship, but also of our lives.”

translations.kjv: Nevertheless the centurion believed the master and the owner of the ship, more than those things which were spoken by Paul.
translations.ylt: but the centurion to the pilot and to the shipowner gave credence more than to the things spoken by Paul;
translations.web: But the centurion gave more heed to the master and to the owner of the ship than to those things which were spoken by Paul.

translations.kjv: And because the haven was not commodious to winter in, the more part advised to depart thence also, if by any means they might attain to Phenice, and there to winter; which is an haven of Crete, and lieth toward the south west and north west.
translations.ylt: and the haven being incommodious to winter in, the more part gave counsel to sail thence also, if by any means they might be able, having attained to Phenice, there to winter, which is a haven of Crete, looking to the south-west and north-west,
translations.web: Because the haven was not suitable to winter in, the majority advised going to sea from there, if by any means they could reach Phoenix and winter there, which is a port of Crete, looking southwest and northwest.

translations.kjv: And when the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, loosing thence, they sailed close by Crete.
translations.ylt: and a south wind blowing softly, having thought they had obtained their purpose, having lifted anchor, they sailed close by Crete,
translations.web: When the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained their purpose, they weighed anchor and sailed along Crete, close to shore.

translations.kjv: But not long after there arose against it a tempestuous wind, called Euroclydon.
translations.ylt: and not long after there arose against it a tempestuous wind, that is called Euroclydon,
translations.web: But before long, a stormy wind beat down from shore, which is called Euroclydon.

translations.kjv: And when the ship was caught, and could not bear up into the wind, we let her drive.
translations.ylt: and the ship being caught, and not being able to bear up against the wind, having given her up, we were borne on,
translations.web: When the ship was caught and couldn’t face the wind, we gave way to it and were driven along.

translations.kjv: And running under a certain island which is called Clauda, we had much work to come by the boat:
translations.ylt: and having run under a certain little isle, called Clauda, we were hardly able to become masters of the boat,
translations.web: Running under the lee of a small island called Clauda, we were able, with difficulty, to secure the boat.

translations.kjv: Which when they had taken up, they used helps, undergirding the ship; and, fearing lest they should fall into the quicksands, strake sail, and so were driven.
translations.ylt: which having taken up, they were using helps, undergirding the ship, and fearing lest they may fall on the quicksand, having let down the mast--so were borne on.
translations.web: After they had hoisted it up, they used cables to help reinforce the ship. Fearing that they would run aground on the Syrtis sand bars, they lowered the sea anchor, and so were driven along.

translations.kjv: And we being exceedingly tossed with a tempest, the next day they lightened the ship;
translations.ylt: And we, being exceedingly tempest-tossed, the succeeding day they were making a clearing,
translations.web: As we labored exceedingly with the storm, the next day they began to throw things overboard.

translations.kjv: And the third day we cast out with our own hands the tackling of the ship.
translations.ylt: and on the third day with our own hands the tackling of the ship we cast out,
translations.web: On the third day, they threw out the ship’s tackle with their own hands.

translations.kjv: And when neither sun nor stars in many days appeared, and no small tempest lay on us, all hope that we should be saved was then taken away.
translations.ylt: and neither sun nor stars appearing for more days, and not a little tempest lying upon us, thenceforth all hope was taken away of our being saved.
translations.web: When neither sun nor stars shone on us for many days, and no small storm pressed on us, all hope that we would be saved was now taken away.

translations.kjv: But after long abstinence Paul stood forth in the midst of them, and said, Sirs, ye should have hearkened unto me, and not have loosed from Crete, and to have gained this harm and loss.
translations.ylt: And there having been long fasting, then Paul having stood in the midst of them, said, `It behoved you, indeed, O men--having hearkened to me--not to set sail from Crete, and to save this hurt and damage;
translations.web: When they had been long without food, Paul stood up in the middle of them and said, “Sirs, you should have listened to me, and not have set sail from Crete and have gotten this injury and loss.

translations.kjv: And now I exhort you to be of good cheer: for there shall be no loss of any man’s life among you, but of the ship.
translations.ylt: and now I exhort you to be of good cheer, for there shall be no loss of life among you--but of the ship;
translations.web: Now I exhort you to cheer up, for there will be no loss of life among you, but only of the ship.

translations.kjv: For there stood by me this night the angel of God, whose I am, and whom I serve,
translations.ylt: for there stood by me this night a messenger of God--whose I am, and whom I serve--
translations.web: For there stood by me this night an angel, belonging to the God whose I am and whom I serve,

translations.kjv: Saying, Fear not, Paul; thou must be brought before Cesar: and, lo, God hath given thee all them that sail with thee.
translations.ylt: saying, Be not afraid Paul; before Caesar it behoveth thee to stand; and, lo, God hath granted to thee all those sailing with thee;
translations.web: saying, ‘Don’t be afraid, Paul. You must stand before Caesar. Behold, God has granted you all those who sail with you.’

translations.kjv: Wherefore, sirs, be of good cheer: for I believe God, that it shall be even as it was told me.
translations.ylt: wherefore be of good cheer, men! for I believe God, that so it shall be, even as it hath been spoken to me,
translations.web: Therefore, sirs, cheer up! For I believe God, that it will be just as it has been spoken to me.

translations.kjv: Howbeit we must be cast upon a certain island.
translations.ylt: and on a certain island it behoveth us to be cast.'
translations.web: But we must run aground on a certain island.”

translations.kjv: But when the fourteenth night was come, as we were driven up and down in Adria, about midnight the shipmen deemed that they drew near to some country;
translations.ylt: And when the fourteenth night came--we being borne up and down in the Adria--toward the middle of the night the sailors were supposing that some country drew nigh to them;
translations.web: But when the fourteenth night had come, as we were driven back and forth in the Adriatic Sea, about midnight the sailors surmised that they were drawing near to some land.

translations.kjv: And sounded, and found it twenty fathoms: and when they had gone a little further, they sounded again, and found it fifteen fathoms.
translations.ylt: and having sounded they found twenty fathoms, and having gone a little farther, and again having sounded, they found fifteen fathoms,
translations.web: They took soundings and found twenty fathoms. After a little while, they took soundings again, and found fifteen fathoms.

translations.kjv: Then fearing lest we should have fallen upon rocks, they cast four anchors out of the stern, and wished for the day.
translations.ylt: and fearing lest on rough places we may fall, out of the stern having cast four anchors, they were wishing day to come.
translations.web: Fearing that we would run aground on rocky ground, they let go four anchors from the stern, and wished for daylight.

translations.kjv: And as the shipmen were about to flee out of the ship, when they had let down the boat into the sea, under colour as though they would have cast anchors out of the foreship,
translations.ylt: And the sailors seeking to flee out of the ship, and having let down the boat to the sea, in pretence as if out of the foreship they are about to cast anchors,
translations.web: As the sailors were trying to flee out of the ship and had lowered the boat into the sea, pretending that they would lay out anchors from the bow,

translations.kjv: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, Except these abide in the ship, ye cannot be saved.
translations.ylt: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, `If these do not remain in the ship--ye are not able to be saved;'
translations.web: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, “Unless these stay in the ship, you can’t be saved.”

translations.kjv: Then the soldiers cut off the ropes of the boat, and let her fall off.
translations.ylt: then the soldiers did cut off the ropes of the boat, and suffered it to fall off.
translations.web: Then the soldiers cut away the ropes of the boat and let it fall off.

translations.kjv: And while the day was coming on, Paul besought them all to take meat, saying, This day is the fourteenth day that ye have tarried and continued fasting, having taken nothing.
translations.ylt: And till the day was about to be, Paul was calling upon all to partake of nourishment, saying, `Fourteen days to-day, waiting, ye continue fasting, having taken nothing,
translations.web: While the day was coming on, Paul begged them all to take some food, saying, “Today is the fourteenth day that you wait and continue fasting, having taken nothing.

translations.kjv: Wherefore I pray you to take some meat: for this is for your health: for there shall not an hair fall from the head of any of you.
translations.ylt: wherefore I call upon you to take nourishment, for this is for your safety, for of not one of you shall a hair from the head fall;'
translations.web: Therefore I beg you to take some food, for this is for your safety; for not a hair will perish from any of your heads.”

translations.kjv: And when he had thus spoken, he took bread, and gave thanks to God in presence of them all: and when he had broken it, he began to eat.
translations.ylt: and having said these things, and having taken bread, he gave thanks to God before all, and having broken it, he began to eat;
translations.web: When he had said this and had taken bread, he gave thanks to God in the presence of all; then he broke it and began to eat.

translations.kjv: Then were they all of good cheer, and they also took some meat.
translations.ylt: and all having become of good cheer, themselves also took food,
translations.web: Then they all cheered up, and they also took food.

translations.kjv: And we were in all in the ship two hundred threescore and sixteen souls.
translations.ylt: (and we were--all the souls in the ship--two hundred, seventy and six),
translations.web: In all, we were two hundred seventy-six souls on the ship.

translations.kjv: And when they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, and cast out the wheat into the sea.
translations.ylt: and having eaten sufficient nourishment, they were lightening the ship, casting forth the wheat into the sea.
translations.web: When they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, throwing out the wheat into the sea.

translations.kjv: And when it was day, they knew not the land: but they discovered a certain creek with a shore, into the which they were minded, if it were possible, to thrust in the ship.
translations.ylt: And when the day came, they were not discerning the land, but a certain creek were perceiving having a beach, into which they took counsel, if possible, to thrust forward the ship,
translations.web: When it was day, they didn’t recognize the land, but they noticed a certain bay with a beach, and they decided to try to drive the ship onto it.

translations.kjv: And when they had taken up the anchors, they committed themselves unto the sea, and loosed the rudder bands, and hoised up the mainsail to the wind, and made toward shore.
translations.ylt: and the anchors having taken up, they were committing it to the sea, at the same time--having loosed the bands of the rudders, and having hoisted up the mainsail to the wind--they were making for the shore,
translations.web: Casting off the anchors, they left them in the sea, at the same time untying the rudder ropes. Hoisting up the foresail to the wind, they made for the beach.

translations.kjv: And falling into a place where two seas met, they ran the ship aground; and the forepart stuck fast, and remained unmoveable, but the hinder part was broken with the violence of the waves.
translations.ylt: and having fallen into a place of two seas, they ran the ship aground, and the fore-part, indeed, having stuck fast, did remain immoveable, but the hinder-part was broken by the violence of the waves.
translations.web: But coming to a place where two seas met, they ran the vessel aground. The bow struck and remained immovable, but the stern began to break up by the violence of the waves.

translations.kjv: And the soldiers’ counsel was to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim out, and escape.
translations.ylt: And the soldiers' counsel was that they should kill the prisoners, lest any one having swam out should escape,
translations.web: The soldiers’ counsel was to kill the prisoners, so that none of them would swim out and escape.

translations.kjv: But the centurion, willing to save Paul, kept them from their purpose; and commanded that they which could swim should cast themselves first into the sea, and get to land:
translations.ylt: but the centurion, wishing to save Paul, hindered them from the counsel, and did command those able to swim, having cast themselves out first--to get unto the land,
translations.web: But the centurion, desiring to save Paul, stopped them from their purpose, and commanded that those who could swim should throw themselves overboard first to go toward the land;

translations.kjv: And the rest, some on boards, and some on broken pieces of the ship. And so it came to pass, that they escaped all safe to land.
translations.ylt: and the rest, some indeed upon boards, and some upon certain things of the ship; and thus it came to pass that all came safe unto the land.
translations.web: and the rest should follow, some on planks and some on other things from the ship. So they all escaped safely to the land.

translations.kjv: And when they were escaped, then they knew that the island was called Melita.
translations.ylt: And having been saved, then they knew that the island is called Melita,
translations.web: When we had escaped, then they learned that the island was called Malta.

translations.kjv: And the barbarous people shewed us no little kindness: for they kindled a fire, and received us every one, because of the present rain, and because of the cold.
translations.ylt: and the foreigners were shewing us no ordinary kindness, for having kindled a fire, they received us all, because of the pressing rain, and because of the cold;
translations.web: The natives showed us uncommon kindness; for they kindled a fire and received us all, because of the present rain and because of the cold.

translations.kjv: And when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks, and laid them on the fire, there came a viper out of the heat, and fastened on his hand.
translations.ylt: but Paul having gathered together a quantity of sticks, and having laid them upon the fire, a viper--out of the heat having come--did fasten on his hand.
translations.web: But when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks and laid them on the fire, a viper came out because of the heat and fastened on his hand.

translations.kjv: And when the barbarians saw the venomous beast hang on his hand, they said among themselves, No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he hath escaped the sea, yet vengeance suffereth not to live.
translations.ylt: And when the foreigners saw the beast hanging from his hand, they said unto one another, `Certainly this man is a murderer, whom, having been saved out of the sea, the justice did not suffer to live;'
translations.web: When the natives saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said to one another, “No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he has escaped from the sea, yet Justice has not allowed to live.”

translations.kjv: And he shook off the beast into the fire, and felt no harm.
translations.ylt: he then, indeed, having shaken off the beast into the fire, suffered no evil,
translations.web: However he shook off the creature into the fire, and wasn’t harmed.

translations.kjv: Howbeit they looked when he should have swollen, or fallen down dead suddenly: but after they had looked a great while, and saw no harm come to him, they changed their minds, and said that he was a god.
translations.ylt: and they were expecting him to be about to be inflamed, or to fall down suddenly dead, and they, expecting it a long time, and seeing nothing uncommon happening to him, changing their minds, said he was a god.
translations.web: But they expected that he would have swollen or fallen down dead suddenly, but when they watched for a long time and saw nothing bad happen to him, they changed their minds and said that he was a god.

translations.kjv: In the same quarters were possessions of the chief man of the island, whose name was Publius; who received us, and lodged us three days courteously.
translations.ylt: And in the neighbourhood of that place were lands of the principal man of the island, by name Publius, who, having received us, three days did courteously lodge us;
translations.web: Now in the neighborhood of that place were lands belonging to the chief man of the island, named Publius, who received us and courteously entertained us for three days.

translations.kjv: And it came to pass, that the father of Publius lay sick of a fever and of a bloody flux: to whom Paul entered in, and prayed, and laid his hands on him, and healed him.
translations.ylt: and it came to pass, the father of Publius with feverish heats and dysentery pressed, was laid, unto whom Paul having entered, and having prayed, having laid his hands on him, healed him;
translations.web: The father of Publius lay sick of fever and dysentery. Paul entered in to him, prayed, and laying his hands on him, healed him.

translations.kjv: So when this was done, others also, which had diseases in the island, came, and were healed:
translations.ylt: this, therefore, being done, the others also in the island having infirmities were coming and were healed;
translations.web: Then when this was done, the rest also who had diseases in the island came and were cured.

translations.kjv: Who also honoured us with many honours; and when we departed, they laded us with such things as were necessary.
translations.ylt: who also with many honours did honour us, and we setting sail--they were lading us with the things that were necessary.
translations.web: They also honored us with many honors; and when we sailed, they put on board the things that we needed.

translations.kjv: And after three months we departed in a ship of Alexandria, which had wintered in the isle, whose sign was Castor and Pollux.
translations.ylt: And after three months, we set sail in a ship (that had wintered in the isle) of Alexandria, with the sign Dioscuri,
translations.web: After three months, we set sail in a ship of Alexandria which had wintered in the island, whose figurehead was “The Twin Brothers.”

translations.kjv: And landing at Syracuse, we tarried there three days.
translations.ylt: and having landed at Syracuse, we remained three days,
translations.web: Touching at Syracuse, we stayed there three days.

translations.kjv: And from thence we fetched a compass, and came to Rhegium: and after one day the south wind blew, and we came the next day to Puteoli:
translations.ylt: thence having gone round, we came to Rhegium, and after one day, a south wind having sprung up, the second day we came to Puteoli;
translations.web: From there we circled around and arrived at Rhegium. After one day, a south wind sprang up, and on the second day we came to Puteoli,

translations.kjv: Where we found brethren, and were desired to tarry with them seven days: and so we went toward Rome.
translations.ylt: where, having found brethren, we were called upon to remain with them seven days, and thus to Rome we came;
translations.web: where we found brothers, and were entreated to stay with them for seven days. So we came to Rome.

translations.kjv: And from thence, when the brethren heard of us, they came to meet us as far as Appii forum, and The three taverns: whom when Paul saw, he thanked God, and took courage.
translations.ylt: and thence, the brethren having heard the things concerning us, came forth to meet us, unto Appii Forum, and Three Taverns--whom Paul having seen, having given thanks to God, took courage.
translations.web: From there the brothers, when they heard of us, came to meet us as far as The Market of Appius and The Three Taverns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and took courage.

translations.kjv: And when we came to Rome, the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard: but Paul was suffered to dwell by himself with a soldier that kept him.
translations.ylt: And when we came to Rome, the centurion delivered up the prisoners to the captain of the barrack, but Paul was suffered to remain by himself, with the soldier guarding him.
translations.web: When we entered into Rome, the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard, but Paul was allowed to stay by himself with the soldier who guarded him.

translations.kjv: And it came to pass, that after three days Paul called the chief of the Jews together: and when they were come together, he said unto them, Men and brethren, though I have committed nothing against the people, or customs of our fathers, yet was I delivered prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans.
translations.ylt: And it came to pass after three days, Paul called together those who are the principal men of the Jews, and they having come together, he said unto them: `Men, brethren, I--having done nothing contrary to the people, or to the customs of the fathers--a prisoner from Jerusalem, was delivered up to the hands of the Romans;
translations.web: After three days Paul called together those who were the leaders of the Jews. When they had come together, he said to them, “I, brothers, though I had done nothing against the people or the customs of our fathers, still was delivered prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans,

translations.kjv: Who, when they had examined me, would have let me go, because there was no cause of death in me.
translations.ylt: who, having examined me, were wishing to release me, because of their being no cause of death in me,
translations.web: who, when they had examined me, desired to set me free, because there was no cause of death in me.

translations.kjv: But when the Jews spake against it, I was constrained to appeal unto Cesar; not that I had ought to accuse my nation of.
translations.ylt: and the Jews having spoken against it, I was constrained to appeal unto Caesar--not as having anything to accuse my nation of;
translations.web: But when the Jews spoke against it, I was constrained to appeal to Caesar, not that I had anything about which to accuse my nation.

translations.kjv: For this cause therefore have I called for you, to see you, and to speak with you: because that for the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain.
translations.ylt: for this cause, therefore, I called for you to see and to speak with you, for because of the hope of Israel with this chain I am bound.'
translations.web: For this cause therefore I asked to see you and to speak with you. For because of the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain.”

translations.kjv: And they said unto him, We neither received letters out of Judea concerning thee, neither any of the brethren that came shewed or spake any harm of thee.
translations.ylt: And they said unto him, `We did neither receive letters concerning thee from Judea, nor did any one who came of the brethren declare or speak any evil concerning thee,
translations.web: They said to him, “We neither received letters from Judea concerning you, nor did any of the brothers come here and report or speak any evil of you.

translations.kjv: But we desire to hear of thee what thou thinkest: for as concerning this sect, we know that every where it is spoken against.
translations.ylt: and we think it good from thee to hear what thou dost think, for, indeed, concerning this sect it is known to us that everywhere it is spoken against;'
translations.web: But we desire to hear from you what you think. For, as concerning this sect, it is known to us that everywhere it is spoken against.”

translations.kjv: And when they had appointed him a day, there came many to him into his lodging; to whom he expounded and testified the kingdom of God, persuading them concerning Jesus, both out of the law of Moses, and out of the prophets, from morning till evening.
translations.ylt: and having appointed him a day, they came, more of them unto him, to the lodging, to whom he was expounding, testifying fully the reign of God, persuading them also of the things concerning Jesus, both from the law of Moses, and the prophets, from morning till evening,
translations.web: When they had appointed him a day, many people came to him at his lodging. He explained to them, testifying about God’s Kingdom, and persuading them concerning Jesus, both from the law of Moses and from the prophets, from morning until evening.

translations.kjv: And some believed the things which were spoken, and some believed not.
translations.ylt: and, some, indeed, were believing the things spoken, and some were not believing.
translations.web: Some believed the things which were spoken, and some disbelieved.

translations.kjv: And when they agreed not among themselves, they departed, after that Paul had spoken one word, Well spake the Holy Ghost by Esaias the prophet unto our fathers,
translations.ylt: And not being agreed with one another, they were going away, Paul having spoken one word--`Well did the Holy Spirit speak through Isaiah the prophet unto our fathers,
translations.web: When they didn’t agree among themselves, they departed after Paul had spoken one message: “The Holy Spirit spoke rightly through Isaiah the prophet to our fathers,

translations.kjv: Saying, Go unto this people, and say, Hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing ye shall see, and not perceive:
translations.ylt: saying, Go on unto this people and say, With hearing ye shall hear, and ye shall not understand, and seeing ye shall see, and ye shall not perceive,
translations.web: saying, ‘Go to this people and say, in hearing, you will hear, but will in no way understand. In seeing, you will see, but will in no way perceive.

translations.kjv: For the heart of this people is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes have they closed; lest they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them.
translations.ylt: for made gross was the heart of this people, and with the ears they heard heavily, and their eyes they did close, lest they may see with the eyes, and with the heart may understand, and be turned back, and I may heal them.
translations.web: For this people’s heart has grown callous. Their ears are dull of hearing. Their eyes they have closed. Lest they should see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their heart, and would turn again, then I would heal them.’

translations.kjv: Be it known therefore unto you, that the salvation of God is sent unto the Gentiles, and that they will hear it.
translations.ylt: `Be it known, therefore, to you, that to the nations was sent the salvation of God, these also will hear it;'
translations.web: “Be it known therefore to you that the salvation of God is sent to the nations, and they will listen.”

translations.kjv: And Paul dwelt two whole years in his own hired house, and received all that came in unto him,
translations.ylt: and Paul remained an entire two years in his own hired house, and was receiving all those coming in unto him,
translations.web: Paul stayed two whole years in his own rented house and received all who were coming to him,

translations.kjv: Preaching the kingdom of God, and teaching those things which concern the Lord Jesus Christ, with all confidence, no man forbidding him.
translations.ylt: preaching the reign of God, and teaching the things concerning the Lord Jesus Christ with all boldness--unforbidden.
translations.web: preaching God’s Kingdom and teaching the things concerning the Lord Jesus Christ with all boldness, without hindrance.
